import pytest

from borgstore.constants import DEL_SUFFIX
from borgstore.store import Store


@pytest.fixture
def store(tmp_path):
    store = Store(
        url=f"file://{tmp_path / 'store'}",
        levels={"objects": (0,)},
    )
    store.create()
    # A file backend does not necessarily pre-create configured namespaces.
    # Create the configured, empty namespace through the Store API so that an
    # empty-list test does not depend on behavior for a nonexistent path.
    store.create_levels()
    try:
        with store:
            yield store
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def listed_names(store, *, deleted):
    return [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=deleted)]


def test_list_separates_active_and_soft_deleted_objects_and_preserves_suffix(store):
    store.store("objects/active-one", b"active-one")
    store.store("objects/to-delete-one", b"deleted-one")
    store.store("objects/active-two", b"active-two")
    store.store("objects/to-delete-two", b"deleted-two")

    store.move("objects/to-delete-one", delete=True)
    store.move("objects/to-delete-two", delete=True)

    active = listed_names(store, deleted=False)
    deleted = listed_names(store, deleted=True)

    assert set(active) == {"active-one", "active-two"}
    assert set(deleted) == {
        f"to-delete-one{DEL_SUFFIX}",
        f"to-delete-two{DEL_SUFFIX}",
    }

    # The views must not overlap, and callers must be able to identify the
    # soft-deleted entries from the returned names.
    assert set(active).isdisjoint(deleted)
    assert all(not name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX) for name in active)
    assert all(name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX) for name in deleted)


def test_list_empty_and_all_soft_deleted_namespace(store):
    # Both filters should be empty for an existing namespace with no objects.
    assert listed_names(store, deleted=False) == []
    assert listed_names(store, deleted=True) == []

    store.store("objects/second", b"second")
    store.move("objects/first", delete=True)
    store.move("objects/second", delete=True)

    # Soft deletion must remove entries from the normal view, without making
    # them disappear from the deleted-only view.
    assert listed_names(store, deleted=False) == []
    assert set(listed_names(store, deleted=True)) == {
        f"first{DEL_SUFFIX}",

"""Regression tests for Store.list soft-deletion filtering."""

import pytest

from borgstore.store import Store


@pytest.fixture()
def store(tmp_path):
    store = Store(url=tmp_path.as_uri(), levels={"objects": [0]})
    store.create()
    try:
        yield store
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def test_list_partitions_live_and_soft_deleted_items_and_keeps_suffix(store):
    """deleted=False and deleted=True must return distinct object sets."""
    with store:
        store.store("objects/live-a", b"live-a")
        store.store("objects/deleted-a", b"deleted-a")
        store.store("objects/live-b", b"live-b")
        store.store("objects/deleted-b", b"deleted-b")

        store.move("objects/deleted-a", delete=True)
        store.move("objects/deleted-b", delete=True)

        live_items = list(store.list("objects", deleted=False))
        deleted_items = list(store.list("objects", deleted=True))

    assert [item.name for item in live_items] == ["live-a", "live-b"]
    assert [item.name for item in deleted_items] == ["deleted-a.del", "deleted-b.del"]

    # A caller must be able to distinguish the two result categories.
    assert all(not item.name.endswith(".del") for item in live_items)
    assert all(item.name.endswith(".del") for item in deleted_items)
    assert {item.name for item in live_items}.isdisjoint(
        {item.name for item in deleted_items}
    )


def test_list_all_soft_deleted_items_excludes_them_from_normal_listing(store):
    """When every object is soft-deleted, normal listing is empty."""
    with store:
        store.store("objects/first", b"one")
        store.store("objects/second", b"two")
        store.move("objects/first", delete=True)
        store.move("objects/second", delete=True)

        assert list(store.list("objects", deleted=False)) == []
        assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=True)] == [
            "first.del",
            "second.del",
        ]


def test_list_reflects_undelete_in_the_opposite_filter(store):
    """An undeleted item must leave deleted listings and return to normal ones."""
    with store:
        store.store("objects/item", b"value")
        store.move("objects/item", delete=True)

        assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=False)] == []
        assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=True)] == [
            "item.del"
        ]

        store.move("objects/item", undelete=True)

        assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=False)] == [
            "item"
        ]
        assert list(store.list("objects", deleted=True)) == []

import pytest

from borgstore.constants import DEL_SUFFIX
from borgstore.store import Store

from .test_backends import get_posixfs_test_backend


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "level, normal_names, deleted_names",
    [
        (0, ["normal-a", "normal-b"], ["deleted-a", "deleted-b"]),
        (1, ["a0000001", "b0000002"], ["c0000003", "d0000004"]),
    ],
)
def test_list_partitions_normal_and_soft_deleted_items(tmp_path, level, normal_names, deleted_names):
    """The deleted flag must select exactly one visible state, at every nesting level."""
    store = Store(
        backend=get_posixfs_test_backend(tmp_path),
        levels={"items": [level]},
    )
    store.create()

    try:
        with store:
            for name in normal_names + deleted_names:
                store.store(f"items/{name}", name.encode())

            for name in deleted_names:
                store.move(f"items/{name}", delete=True)

            visible_names = {item.name for item in store.list("items", deleted=False)}
            soft_deleted_names = {item.name for item in store.list("items", deleted=True)}

            # Normal listing must neither expose soft-deleted items nor their
            # former, suffix-less names.
            assert visible_names == set(normal_names)

            # Deleted listing must not include normal items, and retaining the
            # suffix lets callers distinguish the returned state.
            expected_deleted = {name + DEL_SUFFIX for name in deleted_names}
            assert soft_deleted_names == expected_deleted
            assert visible_names.isdisjoint(soft_deleted_names)
            assert all(not name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX) for name in visible_names)
            assert all(name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX) for name in soft_deleted_names)

            # Edge case: once everything is soft-deleted, the normal view is
            # empty and the deleted view contains every object.
            for name in normal_names:
                store.move(f"items/{name}", delete=True)

            assert list(store.list("items", deleted=False)) == []
            assert {item.name for item in store.list("items", deleted=True)} == {
                name + DEL_SUFFIX for name in normal_names + deleted_names
            }

            # Conversely, after undeleting every object there must be no
            # deleted results at all.
            for name in normal_names + deleted_names:
                store.move(f"items/{name}", undelete=True)

            assert {item.name for item in store.list("items", deleted=False)} == set(
                normal_names + deleted_names
            )
            assert list(store.list("items", deleted=True)) == []
    finally:
        store.destroy()

def test_list_separates_live_and_soft_deleted_items_and_preserves_marker(tmp_path, level):

    store = Store(
        url=f"file://{tmp_path}",
        levels={"objects/": [level]},
    )
    store.create()

    try:
        with store:
            deleted_keys = ["00000001", "00000003"]
            live_keys = ["00000002", "00000004"]

            for key in deleted_keys + live_keys:
                store.store(f"objects/{key}", key.encode())

            for key in deleted_keys:
                store.move(f"objects/{key}", delete=True)

            live_items = list(store.list("objects", deleted=False))
            deleted_items = list(store.list("objects", deleted=True))

            # False (and the default) must expose only live objects.
            assert {item.name for item in live_items} == set(live_keys)
            assert {item.name for item in store.list("objects")} == set(live_keys)

            # True must not include live objects, and must retain the marker so
            # callers can tell that these entries are soft-deleted.
            assert {item.name for item in deleted_items} == {
                f"{key}.del" for key in deleted_keys
            }
            assert all(item.name.endswith(".del") for item in deleted_items)
            assert all(not item.name.endswith(".del") for item in live_items)
    finally:
        store.destroy()

            assert {item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=True)} == {

            store.move("objects/first", undelete=True)

            assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=False)] == ["first"]

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
from craft_cli.errors import CraftError

from charmcraft.application.commands.store import PublishLibCommand


class _PublishedLibrary:
    """A Charmhub library revision whose patch is already published."""

    def __init__(self, lib_id: str):
        self.id = lib_id
        self.lib_id = lib_id
        self.library_id = lib_id
        self.api = 1
        self.patch = 1


class _LibraryResults(list):
    """Response compatible with the library-listing shapes used by store APIs."""

    @property
    def libraries(self):
        return self

    @property
    def results(self):
        return self

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        for library in self:
            if key in (library.id, library.lib_id, library.library_id):
                return library
        return default


class _StoreReportingPublishedPatch:
    """Store double reporting a library at LIBAPI 1, LIBPATCH 1."""

    def __init__(self, lib_id: str):
        self._published = _LibraryResults([_PublishedLibrary(lib_id)])
        self.created = []

    def create_library_revision(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.created.append((args, kwargs))

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        # publish-lib obtains existing library data before deciding whether a
        # revision can be created.  Accommodate the public store lookup method
        # names used by supported store-client versions.
        if name.startswith(("get_", "list_", "find_")):
            return lambda *args, **kwargs: self._published
        raise AttributeError(name)


def _write_library(project_dir, lib_id):
    library = project_dir / "lib" / "charms" / "test_charm" / "v1" / "example.py"
    library.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    library.write_text(
        f'''"""Test charm library."""

LIBID = "{lib_id}"
LIBAPI = 1
LIBPATCH = 1
'''
    )


def _parsed_args(command, output_format):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    command.fill_parser(parser)
    args = parser.parse_args([])
    args.format = output_format
    return args


@pytest.mark.parametrize("output_format", [None, "json"])
def test_publish_lib_fails_when_libpatch_is_already_published(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch, output_format
):
    """A rejected LIBPATCH must result in a non-zero command outcome.

    This exercises both normal human output and programmatic output: changing
    output format must not turn a failed publish into a successful CI step.
    """

    lib_id = "12345678-1234-4123-8123-123456789abc"
    _write_library(tmp_path, lib_id)
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)

    store = _StoreReportingPublishedPatch(lib_id)
    command = object.__new__(PublishLibCommand)
    command._services = SimpleNamespace(
        project=SimpleNamespace(name="test-charm"),
        store=store,
    )

    with pytest.raises(CraftError, match="Failed to publish one or more libraries"):
        command.run(_parsed_args(command, output_format))

    # The stale patch is rejected during analysis and must never be submitted
    # as a new library revision.
    assert store.created == []

import argparse

import pytest
from craft_cli.errors import CraftError

from charmcraft.application.commands import store as store_commands


class _RemoteLibrary:
    """A minimal published charm library revision."""

    def __init__(self, library_id: str, patch: int):
        self.id = library_id
        self.library_id = library_id
        self.lib_id = library_id
        self.api = 0
        self.patch = patch


class _LibraryLookupResult(list):
    """Support store methods returning either a library or a revision list."""

    def __init__(self, libraries):
        super().__init__(libraries)
        library = libraries[0] if libraries else None
        self.id = getattr(library, "id", None)
        self.library_id = getattr(library, "library_id", None)
        self.lib_id = getattr(library, "lib_id", None)
        self.api = getattr(library, "api", None)
        self.patch = getattr(library, "patch", None)


class _FakeStore:
    """Store fake containing a library whose latest patch is already newer."""

    def __init__(self, library_id):
        self.remote_library = _RemoteLibrary(library_id, patch=1)
        self.create_library_revision_calls = []

    def _get_library(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return _LibraryLookupResult([self.remote_library])

    def create_library_revision(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.create_library_revision_calls.append((args, kwargs))

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        # publish-lib has used different library lookup method names over time.
        # All of them must report the already-published patch to this test.
        if "library" in name and name.startswith(("get_", "list_")):
            return self._get_library
        raise AttributeError(name)


def _write_library(path, library_id, patch):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(
        f'''\
LIBID = "{library_id}"
LIBAPI = 0
LIBPATCH = {patch}
''',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("output_format", [None, "json"])
def test_publish_lib_returns_failure_for_rejected_patch(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch, output_format
):
    """A stale LIBPATCH must produce a non-zero command result.

    This includes --format json, which is commonly used by CI callers and
    must not turn a failed publication into a successful process exit.
    """
    library_id = "22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222"
    library_path = tmp_path / "lib" / "charms" / "example" / "v0" / "stale.py"

    # The local patch goes backwards from the currently published patch (1).
    _write_library(library_path, library_id, patch=0)

    fake_store = _FakeStore(library_id)
    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands, "Store", lambda *args, **kwargs: fake_store)

    command = object.__new__(store_commands.PublishLibCommand)
    command._services = SimpleNamespace(
        store=fake_store,
        project=SimpleNamespace(name="example"),
    )

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    command.fill_parser(parser)
    arguments = [str(library_path)]
    if output_format:
        arguments.extend(["--format", output_format])
    parsed_args = parser.parse_args(arguments)

    try:
        result = command.run(parsed_args)
    except CraftError:
        # The application runner converts CraftError into a non-zero exit code.

    else:

        # regression was returning normally (None, hence exit status zero).

    assert fake_store.create_library_revision_calls == []

import argparse
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
from craft_cli import CraftError

from charmcraft.application.commands.store import PublishLibCommand


class _RemoteLibrary:
    """A library revision already published to Charmhub."""

    lib_id = "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
    library_id = lib_id
    id = lib_id
    api = 0
    patch = 1
    revision = patch

    def __getitem__(self, key):
        return getattr(self, key)


class _StoreWithNewerLibrary:
    """Store fake reporting a revision newer than the local one."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.remote_library = _RemoteLibrary()

    def get_library_revision(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return self.remote_library

    def get_library_revisions(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return [self.remote_library]

    def list_library_revisions(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return [self.remote_library]

    def list_libraries(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return [self.remote_library]

    def get_library(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return self.remote_library

    def create_library_revision(self, *args, **kwargs):
        raise AssertionError(
            "A library whose LIBPATCH has gone backwards must not be published"
        )


def _make_command(store):
    """Build a command without requiring the whole application configuration."""
    command = object.__new__(PublishLibCommand)
    command._services = SimpleNamespace(
        store=store,
        # publish-lib uses the project name as the Charmhub owner/name under
        # which the library is being published.
        project=SimpleNamespace(name="test-charm"),
    )
    return command


def _publish_args(command, library_path, output_format):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    command.fill_parser(parser)

    positional_actions = [
        action
        for action in parser._actions
        if not action.option_strings and action.dest != "help"
    ]
    if positional_actions:
        args = parser.parse_args([str(library_path)])
    elif any("--library" in action.option_strings for action in parser._actions):
        args = parser.parse_args(["--library", str(library_path)])
    else:
        args = parser.parse_args([])

    # The failure status must be identical for human and machine-readable
    # output, independently of the common parser's format-option setup.
    args.format = output_format
    return args


@pytest.mark.parametrize("output_format", [None, "json"])
def test_publish_lib_fails_when_local_patch_is_older_than_store(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch, output_format
):
    """A rejected LIBPATCH revision must produce a failing command result.

    Charmhub already has patch 1, while the local library has patch 0.  This
    is the LIBPATCH-going-backwards error described in the issue: it must not
    merely be printed while the command exits successfully.
    """
    library_path = tmp_path / "lib" / "charms" / "example" / "v0" / "example.py"
    library_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    library_path.write_text(
        "\n".join(
            [
                'LIBID = "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"',
                "LIBAPI = 0",
                "LIBPATCH = 0",
                "",
            ]
        )
    )
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)

    command = _make_command(_StoreWithNewerLibrary())
    args = _publish_args(command, library_path, output_format)

    try:
        result = command.run(args)
    except CraftError:
        # CraftError is translated by the command framework to a non-zero
        # process exit status.
        return

    # Returning a non-zero status is also a valid way for a command to report
    # failure. Historically this returned None, which meant exit status 0.
    assert result not in (None, 0)

from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import pytest
from craft_cli.errors import CraftError

from charmcraft.application.commands.store import PublishLibCommand


def _library(*, name: str, patch: int, path: Path) -> SimpleNamespace:
    """Build library metadata used by PublishLibCommand."""
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(f"LIBPATCH = {patch}\n")

    return SimpleNamespace(
        charm_name="test-charm",
        lib_id=f"{name}-id",
        lib_name=name,
        full_name=f"charms.test-charm.v0.{name}",
        api=0,
        patch=patch,
        content=f"LIBPATCH = {patch}\n",
        content_hash=f"{name}-content-{patch}",
        path=path,
    )


def _command() -> PublishLibCommand:
    services = MagicMock()
    services.project.name = "test-charm"
    return PublishLibCommand({"app": MagicMock(), "services": services})


def _assert_command_fails(command: PublishLibCommand, args: SimpleNamespace) -> None:
    """Require a command failure, either as an exception or a non-zero status."""
    try:
        result = command.run(args)
    except CraftError:
        # The application framework converts CraftError to a non-zero CLI exit
        # status, which is the required behavior for CI callers.
        return

    assert result not in (None, 0), (
        "publish-lib reported success despite being unable to publish a library"
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("local_patch", "published_patch"),
    [
        (5, 5),  # LIBPATCH was not bumped.
        (4, 5),  # LIBPATCH was decremented.
    ],
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("output_format", [None, "json"])
def test_publish_lib_invalid_patch_fails(
    tmp_path, local_patch, published_patch, output_format
):
    """A rejected library revision must produce a failing command result."""
    local_library = _library(
        name="broken",
        patch=local_patch,
        path=tmp_path / "lib" / "broken.py",
    )
    published_tip = SimpleNamespace(
        api=0,
        patch=published_patch,
        content_hash="already-published-content",
    )
    args = SimpleNamespace(library=local_library.full_name, format=output_format)

    with (
        patch(
            "charmcraft.application.commands.store.utils.get_lib_info",
            return_value=local_library,
        ),
        patch("charmcraft.application.commands.store.Store") as store_class,
        patch("charmcraft.application.commands.store.emit"),
    ):
        store = store_class.return_value
        store.get_libraries_tips.return_value = {
            (local_library.lib_id, local_library.api): published_tip
        }

        _assert_command_fails(_command(), args)

    # The validation error must prevent a request to create the invalid revision.
    store.create_library_revision.assert_not_called()


def test_publish_all_libs_fails_if_one_library_is_rejected(tmp_path):
    """Publishing all libraries must fail overall when any one cannot publish."""
    valid_library = _library(
        name="valid",
        patch=2,
        # Both files need the same grandparent for the all-libraries path.
        path=tmp_path / "libraries" / "valid.py",
    )
    invalid_library = _library(
        name="outdated",
        patch=4,
        path=tmp_path / "libraries" / "outdated.py",
    )
    args = SimpleNamespace(library=None, format=None)

    with (
        patch(
            "charmcraft.application.commands.store.utils.get_libs_from_tree",
            return_value=[valid_library, invalid_library],
        ),
        patch("charmcraft.application.commands.store.Store") as store_class,
        patch("charmcraft.application.commands.store.emit"),
    ):
        store = store_class.return_value
        store.get_libraries_tips.return_value = {
            # This is a valid next revision.
            (valid_library.lib_id, valid_library.api): SimpleNamespace(
                api=0, patch=1, content_hash="old-valid-content"
            ),
            # This would move LIBPATCH backwards.
            (invalid_library.lib_id, invalid_library.api): SimpleNamespace(
                api=0, patch=5, content_hash="newer-published-content"
            ),
        }

        _assert_command_fails(_command(), args)

    # The invalid library must never be submitted, even in a mixed batch.
    assert all(
        call.args[1] != invalid_library.lib_id
        for call in store.create_library_revision.call_args_list
    )

from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, Mock

import pytest
from craft_cli.errors import CraftError

from charmcraft.application.commands.store import PublishLibCommand


class _PublishedLibraryRevisions(list):
    """A response usable by the different library-revision store APIs."""

    def __init__(self, revision):
        super().__init__([revision])
        self.api = revision.api
        self.patch = revision.patch
        self.revisions = self


class _StoreWithPublishedRevision:
    """Store fake reporting that revision 0.0 was already published."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.create_library_revision = Mock()
        revision = SimpleNamespace(
            api=0,
            patch=0,
            library_id="12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc",
            id="12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc",
        )
        self._published = _PublishedLibraryRevisions(revision)

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        # publish-lib has used more than one Store API name for looking up
        # library revisions. Each lookup must see an already-published 0.0
        # revision so that attempting to publish 0.0 is rejected.
        if "librar" in name.lower():
            return Mock(return_value=self._published)
        raise AttributeError(name)


def _write_library(root: Path) -> Path:
    """Create a valid charm library whose patch was not bumped."""
    library = root / "lib" / "charms" / "example" / "v0" / "sample.py"
    library.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    library.write_text(
        "\n".join(
            [
                '"""Example charm library."""',
                'LIBID = "12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc"',
                "LIBAPI = 0",

def _parsed_publish_args(command: PublishLibCommand, library: Path):
    """Build command arguments in the same way the CLI parser does."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    command.fill_parser(parser)

    required_positionals = [
        action
        for action in parser._actions
        if not action.option_strings and action.required
    ]
    args = parser.parse_args([str(library)] * len(required_positionals))

    if not hasattr(args, "format"):
        args.format = None
    return args

        # publish-lib obtains the charm name from the loaded project before
        # analysing its libraries.
        project=SimpleNamespace(name="example"),
    )
    command = PublishLibCommand({"app": MagicMock(), "services": services})
    args = _parsed_publish_args(command, library)

    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)

    # Publishing the same API/patch as an existing library revision is a
    # normal publish-lib validation failure. It used to be reported but the
    # command then returned successfully (exit status 0).
    with pytest.raises(CraftError, match="Failed to publish one or more libraries"):
        command.run(args)

    store.create_library_revision.assert_not_called()

class _Library:
    """Minimal local/published library data used by PublishLibCommand."""

    def __init__(self, name, patch, path):
        self.name = name
        self.api = 0
        self.patch = patch
        self.content = f"# library {name}\n"
        self.path = path

    def __iter__(self):
        """Support discovery helpers which expect an iterable result."""
        yield self


class _LibraryDiscovery:
    """No-I/O replacement for the command's local-library discovery utility."""

    def __init__(self, library):
        self.library = library

    def __getattr__(self, _name):
        return lambda *args, **kwargs: self.library


def _run_publish_lib(monkeypatch, tmp_path, *, local_patch, published_patch):
    """Run PublishLibCommand with one local and one published library revision."""
    library_name = "charms.test.v0.example"
    library_path = tmp_path / "example.py"
    library_path.write_text("# a real, existing local library file\n")

    local_library = _Library(library_name, local_patch, library_path)
    published_library = _Library(library_name, published_patch, library_path)

    store = MagicMock()
    # Different store lookups are used across compatible charmcraft versions.
    # Supplying both keeps this test focused on command result handling.
    store.list_libraries.return_value = [published_library]
    store.get_library.return_value = published_library

    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands, "Store", MagicMock(return_value=store))
    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands, "utils", _LibraryDiscovery(local_library))

    command = object.__new__(PublishLibCommand)
    command._services = MagicMock()
    command._services.store = store

    args = Namespace(
        library=["src/charm.py"],
        libraries=["src/charm.py"],
        format=None,
    )
    return command.run(args), store


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "local_patch,published_patch",
    [
        (4, 4),  # LIBPATCH was not bumped.
        (4, 5),  # LIBPATCH went backwards.
    ],
)
def test_publish_lib_returns_nonzero_when_store_rejects_patch(
    monkeypatch, tmp_path, local_patch, published_patch

from argparse import Namespace
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import pytest

from charmcraft.application.commands import store as store_commands


def _library_data(tmp_path, *, patch: int):
    """Create parsed charm-library data accepted by publish-lib."""
    library_path = tmp_path / "lib" / "charms" / "test_charm" / "v0" / "example.py"
    library_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    library_path.write_text(f"LIBAPI = 0\nLIBPATCH = {patch}\n")

    return SimpleNamespace(
        lib_id="0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
        api=0,
        patch=patch,
        content=f"LIBAPI = 0\nLIBPATCH = {patch}\n",
        content_hash=f"local-content-at-patch-{patch}",
        full_name="charms.test_charm.v0.example",
        lib_name="example",
        charm_name="test-charm",
        path=library_path,
    )


def _run_publish_lib(
    monkeypatch,
    tmp_path,
    *,
    local_patch: int,
    remote_patch: int,
    output_format=None,
):
    """Run publish-lib against a mocked Charmhub library tip."""
    library = _library_data(tmp_path, patch=local_patch)
    tip = SimpleNamespace(
        api=0,
        patch=remote_patch,
        # A differing hash means an equal LIBPATCH is not a harmless attempt
        # to publish unchanged content.
        content_hash="published-content",
    )

    store = MagicMock()
    store.get_libraries_tips.return_value = {(library.lib_id, library.api): tip}

    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands, "Store", MagicMock(return_value=store))
    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands.env, "get_store_config", MagicMock())
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        store_commands.utils, "get_lib_info", MagicMock(return_value=library)
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands.emit, "message", MagicMock())
    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands.emit, "debug", MagicMock())

    command = store_commands.PublishLibCommand(
        {
            "app": MagicMock(),
            "services": SimpleNamespace(project=SimpleNamespace(name="test-charm")),
        }
    )
    result = command.run(
        Namespace(
            library="charms.test_charm.v0.example",
            format=output_format,
        )
    )
    return result, store


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("local_patch", "remote_patch", "output_format"),
    [
        # LIBPATCH was moved backwards from the version already published.
        (4, 5, None),
        # The library changed but LIBPATCH was not bumped. Machine-readable
        # output must not cause this failure to become a successful exit.
        (5, 5, "json"),
    ],
)
def test_publish_lib_returns_failure_status_for_invalid_libpatch(
    monkeypatch, tmp_path, local_patch, remote_patch, output_format
):
    """A rejected library publish must produce a non-zero command status."""
    result, store = _run_publish_lib(
        monkeypatch,
        tmp_path,
        local_patch=local_patch,
        remote_patch=remote_patch,
        output_format=output_format,
    )

    assert result == 1
    store.create_library_revision.assert_not_called()


def test_publish_lib_keeps_success_status_when_libpatch_is_incremented(
    monkeypatch, tmp_path
):
    """A valid new library revision must not be reported as a failure."""
    result, store = _run_publish_lib(
        monkeypatch,
        tmp_path,
        local_patch=6,
        remote_patch=5,
    )

    # Commands without an explicit integer return are normalized by the CLI to
    # a successful process exit status.
    assert result in (None, 0)
    store.create_library_revision.assert_called_once()

from __future__ import annotations

from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA


def test_multi_base_charm_artifact_names_are_github_safe(tmp_path, service_factory):
    """Multi-base platform labels must not put ':' in packed charm filenames."""
    project_dir = tmp_path / "project"
    project_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    destination = tmp_path / "artifacts"
    destination.mkdir()
    prime_dir = tmp_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("charm payload")

    platforms = (
        ("ubuntu@22.04:amd64", "amd64"),
        ("ubuntu@22.04:arm64", "arm64"),
    )
    project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "multi-base-charm",
            "summary": "A multi-base test charm",
            "description": "A multi-base test charm",
            "type": "charm",
            "platforms": {platform: None for platform, _ in platforms},
            "parts": {},
        }
    )

    package_names = []
    for platform, architecture in platforms:
        package_service = services.PackageService(
            app=APP_METADATA,
            project=project,
            services=service_factory,
            project_dir=project_dir,
            build_plan=[
                BuildInfo(
                    platform=platform,
                    build_on=architecture,
                    build_for=architecture,
                    base=BaseName("ubuntu", "22.04"),
                )
            ],
        )

        packages = package_service.pack(prime_dir, destination)

        assert len(packages) == 1
        package = packages[0]
        package_names.append(package.name)

        assert package.exists()
        assert package.suffix == ".charm"
        assert package.name.startswith("multi-base-charm_")
        assert package.name.endswith(f"{architecture}.charm")
        assert ":" not in package.name

        # ':' makes the filename unsuitable for GitHub Actions artifacts/releases.
        assert not set(package.name).intersection('<>:"/\\|?*')

        original_name = f"multi-base-charm_{platform}.charm"

    assert len(set(package_names)) == len(platforms)

    recorded_packages = (
        project_dir / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt"
    ).read_text().splitlines()
    assert recorded_packages == package_names
    assert all(":" not in package_name for package_name in recorded_packages)

from io import StringIO

from csv2md.table import Table


def _split_markdown_table_row(line):
    """Split a markdown table row only at structural (unescaped) pipes."""
    assert line.startswith("|")
    assert line.endswith("|")

    parts = []
    current = []
    index = 0

    while index < len(line):
        character = line[index]

        # A backslash escapes the following markdown character. In
        # particular, an odd number of backslashes before a pipe protects it.
        if character == "\\" and index + 1 < len(line):
            current.append(character)
            current.append(line[index + 1])
            index += 2
            continue

        if character == "|":
            parts.append("".join(current))
            current = []
        else:
            current.append(character)

        index += 1

    parts.append("".join(current))

    # csv2md emits an opening and closing structural pipe.
    assert parts[0] == ""
    assert parts[-1] == ""

    return [part.strip() for part in parts[1:-1]]


def _render_markdown_cell(source):
    """Decode the markdown constructs relevant to escaped table pipes."""
    rendered = []
    index = 0

    while index < len(source):
        if source.startswith("|", index):
            rendered.append("|")
            index += len("|")
        elif (
            source[index] == "\\"
            and index + 1 < len(source)
            and source[index + 1] in ("\\", "|")
        ):
            rendered.append(source[index + 1])
            index += 2
        else:
            rendered.append(source[index])
            index += 1

    return "".join(rendered)


def test_markdown_table_keeps_pipe_containing_csv_items_as_single_cells():
    csv_input = StringIO(
        '"a","b"\n'
        '"foo","bar"\n'
        '"test|with|pipe|symbol","baz"\n'
        '"test\\|with\\|already\\|escaped","baz"\n'
        '"test|with|html|entity","baz"\n'
        '"|starts-with-pipe","ends-with-pipe|"\n'
        '"two||adjacent||pipes","plain"\n'
    )

    markdown = Table.parse_csv(csv_input).markdown()
    lines = markdown.splitlines()

    # Header, separator, and one row for each CSV record.
    assert len(lines) == 8

    expected_rows = [
        ["a", "b"],
        ["foo", "bar"],
        ["test|with|pipe|symbol", "baz"],
        # The backslashes are CSV data and must remain visible after the
        # markdown is rendered; consequently the generated markdown must not
        # treat them as the only escaping backslashes for the pipes.
        [r"test\|with\|already\|escaped", "baz"],
        ["test|with|html|entity", "baz"],
        ["|starts-with-pipe", "ends-with-pipe|"],
        ["two||adjacent||pipes", "plain"],
    ]

    # Every data row must still have exactly two structural table cells.
    # This permits either markdown's \| form or the | HTML entity form,
    # while rejecting an unescaped pipe that creates extra columns.
    markdown_rows = [lines[0], *lines[2:]]
    for markdown_row, expected_cells in zip(markdown_rows, expected_rows):
        source_cells = _split_markdown_table_row(markdown_row)
        assert len(source_cells) == 2
        assert [_render_markdown_cell(cell) for cell in source_cells] == expected_cells

import io

from csv2md.table import Table


def _markdown_cells(line):
    """Extract the (padded) cells from one csv2md markdown row."""
    assert line.startswith("| ")
    assert line.endswith(" |")
    return [cell.rstrip() for cell in line[2:-2].split(" | ")]


def _decode_table_cell(cell):
    """Decode the relevant markdown escapes while rejecting bare pipes."""
    decoded = []
    index = 0

    while index < len(cell):
        if cell.startswith("|", index):
            decoded.append("|")
            index += len("|")
        elif cell.startswith("\\\\", index):
            # Markdown's escaped-backslash form represents one literal
            # backslash. It must be handled before the backslash-pipe form.
            decoded.append("\\")
            index += 2
        elif cell.startswith(r"\|", index):
            decoded.append("|")
            index += 2
        else:
            assert cell[index] != "|", "found an unescaped pipe inside a table cell"
            decoded.append(cell[index])
            index += 1

    return "".join(decoded)


def test_markdown_escapes_pipes_in_headers_and_data_cells():
    table = Table.parse_csv(
        io.StringIO(
            '"column|name","other"\n'
            '"one|two|three","left|right"\n'
        )
    )

    lines = table.markdown().splitlines()
    header = _markdown_cells(lines[0])
    row = _markdown_cells(lines[2])

    # A pipe may be represented by either \\| or |, but it must not be
    # left as a markdown table delimiter.
    assert len(header) == 2
    assert len(row) == 2
    assert _decode_table_cell(header[0]) == "column|name"
    assert _decode_table_cell(header[1]) == "other"
    assert _decode_table_cell(row[0]) == "one|two|three"
    assert _decode_table_cell(row[1]) == "left|right"


def test_markdown_preserves_literal_backslashes_before_pipes():
    # The issue's reproducer includes already backslash-escaped pipes.  CSV
    # still treats the backslash as item content, so generated markdown must
    # represent both the literal backslash and the literal pipe without
    # allowing the pipe to become a column boundary.
    source_value = r"already\|escaped\|pipe"
    table = Table.parse_csv(
        io.StringIO(
            '"item","value"\n'
            '"already\\|escaped\\|pipe","ok"\n'
        )
    )

    row = _markdown_cells(table.markdown().splitlines()[2])

    assert len(row) == 2
    assert _decode_table_cell(row[0]) == source_value
    assert _decode_table_cell(row[1]) == "ok"


def test_markdown_keeps_html_escaped_pipes_within_the_same_cell():
    # HTML character references are another documented markdown-safe form and
    # must not be split by conversion.
    table = Table.parse_csv(
        io.StringIO(
            '"item","value"\n'
            '"test|with|escaped|pipe","baz"\n'
        )
    )

    row = _markdown_cells(table.markdown().splitlines()[2])

    assert len(row) == 2
    assert _decode_table_cell(row[0]) == "test|with|escaped|pipe"
    assert _decode_table_cell(row[1]) == "baz"

"""Regression tests for safe multi-base charm artifact names."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
import zipfile

import pytest
from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "platform",
    [
        pytest.param("ubuntu@22.04:amd64", id="amd64"),
        pytest.param("ubuntu@22.04:arm64", id="arm64"),
    ],
)
def test_pack_multibase_charm_artifact_name_has_no_colon(
    new_path: pathlib.Path,
    service_factory,
    platform: str,
):
    """Multi-base platform labels must produce GitHub-uploadable artifact names.

    Platform labels use ``:`` to separate the base from the architecture, but
    ``:`` is not accepted in GitHub Actions artifact or release filenames.
    """
    architecture = platform.rsplit(":", maxsplit=1)[1]
    project_dir = new_path / "project"
    project_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    prime_dir = new_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("charm payload")
    destination = new_path / "artifacts"
    destination.mkdir()

    project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "multi-base-charm",
            "summary": "A multi-base charm",
            "description": "A charm built for more than one platform.",
            "type": "charm",
            "platforms": {platform: None},
            "parts": {},
        }
    )
    build_plan = [
        BuildInfo(
            platform=platform,
            build_on=architecture,
            build_for=architecture,
            base=BaseName("ubuntu", "22.04"),
        )
    ]
    package_service = services.PackageService(
        app=APP_METADATA,
        project=project,
        services=service_factory,
        project_dir=project_dir,
        build_plan=build_plan,
    )

    packages = package_service.pack(prime_dir, destination)

    assert len(packages) == 1
    charm_path = packages[0]
    assert charm_path.exists()
    assert charm_path.suffix == ".charm"
    assert charm_path.name.startswith("multi-base-charm_")
    assert ":" not in charm_path.name

    # Charmcraft records the artifact name for consumers that pack into a
    # separate destination directory; this recorded upload path must be safe too.
    assert (project_dir / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt").read_text().splitlines() == [
        charm_path.name
    ]
    assert all(":" not in artifact.name for artifact in destination.glob("*.charm"))

    with zipfile.ZipFile(charm_path) as charm:
        assert charm.read("payload.txt") == b"charm payload"

import pytest

from ucumvert import PintUcumRegistry, ucum_preprocessor


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("ucum_code", "target_unit", "expected_magnitude"),
    [
        ("m[IU]", "international_unit", 1e-3),
        ("m[IU]/L", "international_unit / liter", 1e-3),
        ("k[IU]/L", "international_unit / liter", 1e3),
        # A prefix before a bracketed UCUM unit must remain a prefix and must
        # not be interpreted as an unrelated Pint unit (such as meter).
        ("u[IU]/L", "international_unit / liter", 1e-6),
        # Scaling must be retained independently on both sides of a compound
        # UCUM expression: milli-IU per milliliter equals IU per liter.
        ("m[IU]/mL", "international_unit / liter", 1.0),
    ],
)
def test_prefixed_international_units_have_prefix_scale_not_length_dimension(
    ucum_code, target_unit, expected_magnitude
):
    ureg = PintUcumRegistry()

    result = ureg.from_ucum(ucum_code).to(target_unit)

    assert result.magnitude == pytest.approx(expected_magnitude)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("ucum_code", "expected_magnitude"),
    [
        ("m[IU]/L", 1e-3),
        ("k[IU]/L", 1e3),
    ],
)
def test_ucum_preprocessor_handles_prefixed_international_units(
    ucum_code, expected_magnitude
):
    """The public UCUM string preprocessor must emit a parseable Pint expression."""
    ureg = PintUcumRegistry()
    target_unit = ureg("international_unit / liter").units
    ureg.preprocessors.append(ucum_preprocessor)

    result = ureg(ucum_code).to(target_unit)

    assert result.magnitude == pytest.approx(expected_magnitude)

import io

from csv2md.table import Table


def _markdown_cells(line):
    """Split a Markdown table row while preserving backslash-escaped pipes."""
    assert line.startswith("| ")
    assert line.endswith(" |")

    cells = []
    cell = []
    backslashes = 0

    for character in line[2:-2]:
        if character == "|" and backslashes % 2 == 0:
            cells.append("".join(cell).rstrip())
            cell = []
            backslashes = 0
            continue

        cell.append(character)
        if character == "\\":
            backslashes += 1
        else:
            backslashes = 0

    cells.append("".join(cell).rstrip())
    return cells


def test_markdown_escapes_pipes_in_csv_headers_and_items():
    table = Table.parse_csv(
        io.StringIO(
            '"head|er",kind\n'
            '"one|pipe",ordinary\n'
            '"|at both ends|",edge\n'
            '"many|pipes|in|one|item",multiple\n'
        )
    )

    rows = [_markdown_cells(line) for line in table.markdown().splitlines()]

    # Content pipes must not create additional Markdown columns.
    assert len(rows[0]) == 2
    assert all(len(row) == 2 for row in rows[2:])

    # Backslash escaping is the preferred representation in the issue.
    assert rows[0][0] == r"head\|er"
    assert rows[2][0] == r"one\|pipe"
    assert rows[3][0] == r"\|at both ends\|"
    assert rows[4][0] == r"many\|pipes\|in\|one\|item"


def test_markdown_does_not_reescape_an_already_escaped_pipe():
    # The issue's reproducer includes values which already contain Markdown's
    # pipe escape.  It is already safe table content and must remain so:
    # turning \| into \\\| leaves a visible backslash after rendering.
    table = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO('value,kind\n"already\\|escaped",existing\n'))

    rows = [_markdown_cells(line) for line in table.markdown().splitlines()]

    assert rows[2] == [r"already\|escaped", "existing"]


def test_markdown_keeps_html_pipe_entities_unchanged():
    # HTML's character entity is the other safe representation explicitly
    # mentioned by the issue and must not be altered.
    table = Table.parse_csv(
        io.StringIO('value,kind\n"test|with|pipe",entity\n')
    )

    rows = [_markdown_cells(line) for line in table.markdown().splitlines()]

    assert rows[2] == ["test|with|pipe", "entity"]

import io

from csv2md.table import Table


def _unescaped_pipe_count(markdown_line):
    """Count pipe characters that can act as Markdown table delimiters."""
    count = 0
    for index, char in enumerate(markdown_line):
        if char != "|":
            continue

        backslashes = 0
        cursor = index - 1
        while cursor >= 0 and markdown_line[cursor] == "\\":
            backslashes += 1
            cursor -= 1

        if backslashes % 2 == 0:
            count += 1
    return count


def test_markdown_escapes_pipes_in_csv_items_without_creating_columns():
    csv_data = (
        '"a","b"\n'
        '"foo","bar"\n'
        '"test|with|pipe|symbol","baz"\n'
        '"test\\|with\\|pipe\\|symbol","baz"\n'
        '"test|with|escaped|pipe","baz"\n'
    )

    markdown_lines = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data)).markdown().splitlines()

    raw_pipe_row = markdown_lines[3]
    preescaped_pipe_row = markdown_lines[4]
    html_entity_row = markdown_lines[5]

    # Raw pipes from CSV data must be represented safely in Markdown.
    assert (
        r"test\|with\|pipe\|symbol" in raw_pipe_row
        or "test|with|pipe|symbol" in raw_pipe_row
    )

    # A CSV field that contains backslashes as well as pipes must also remain
    # one table item rather than being split into additional columns.
    assert "test" in preescaped_pipe_row
    assert "with" in preescaped_pipe_row
    assert "pipe" in preescaped_pipe_row
    assert "symbol" in preescaped_pipe_row

    # Already HTML-escaped pipes are valid Markdown table content and should
    # not be altered into literal delimiter pipes.
    assert "test|with|escaped|pipe" in html_entity_row

    # Every line of this two-column table has exactly three structural pipes:
    # opening border, column separator, and closing border.
    for line in markdown_lines:
        assert _unescaped_pipe_count(line) == 3


def test_markdown_escapes_pipe_characters_in_header_cells_too():
    table = Table([
        ["name|with|pipes", "value"],
        ["ordinary", "data"],
    ])

    markdown_lines = table.markdown().splitlines()

    assert (
        r"name\|with\|pipes" in markdown_lines[0]
        or "name|with|pipes" in markdown_lines[0]
    )

    for line in markdown_lines:
        assert _unescaped_pipe_count(line) == 3

"""Regression tests for artifact filenames generated from platform labels."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest

from charmcraft.services.package import PackageService


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("platform", "expected_name"),
    [
        ("ubuntu@22.04:amd64", "example-charm_ubuntu@22.04-amd64.charm"),
        ("ubuntu@22.04:arm64", "example-charm_ubuntu@22.04-arm64.charm"),
    ],
)
def test_multi_base_charm_artifact_name_is_github_safe(
    tmp_path: pathlib.Path, platform: str, expected_name: str
) -> None:
    """Platform-qualified charm artifacts must not contain GitHub-invalid colons."""
    service = object.__new__(PackageService)
    service._project = SimpleNamespace(name="example-charm")
    service._platform = platform

    charm_path = service.get_charm_path(tmp_path)

    assert charm_path == tmp_path / expected_name
    assert ":" not in charm_path.name
    assert charm_path.suffix == ".charm"


def test_platform_without_colon_keeps_its_existing_artifact_name(
    tmp_path: pathlib.Path,
) -> None:
    """Sanitising multi-base labels must not alter ordinary platform labels."""
    service = object.__new__(PackageService)
    service._project = SimpleNamespace(name="example-charm")
    service._platform = "amd64"

    assert service.get_charm_path(tmp_path).name == "example-charm_amd64.charm"

from csv2md.table import Table


def test_cell_pipes_are_escaped_and_rendered_rows_remain_column_aligned():
    """Pipes in any cell must be safe Markdown without breaking table layout."""
    table = Table([
        ["head|er", "plain"],
        ["|at the start", "middle|pipe"],
        ["two||adjacent", "at the end|"],
    ])

    markdown = table.markdown()
    lines = markdown.splitlines()

    # The issue permits either a Markdown backslash escape or the HTML entity.
    # Check headers and every data-row position, rather than only one common
    # unescaped-pipe case.
    assert "head\\|er" in markdown or "head|er" in markdown
    assert "\\|at the start" in markdown or "|at the start" in markdown
    assert "middle\\|pipe" in markdown or "middle|pipe" in markdown
    assert "two\\|\\|adjacent" in markdown or "two||adjacent" in markdown
    assert "at the end\\|" in markdown or "at the end|" in markdown

    # Escaping adds characters to the serialized cell.  Width calculation must
    # account for those characters, otherwise the visual table no longer has
    # consistently aligned column boundaries.
    first_column_boundaries = [line.find(" | ", 2) for line in lines]
    assert -1 not in first_column_boundaries
    assert len(set(first_column_boundaries)) == 1, markdown


def test_existing_backslash_escaped_pipes_remain_valid_markdown_escapes():
    """CSV values already containing \\| must not gain visible backslashes."""
    table = Table([
        ["item", "value"],
        [r"already\|escaped", "one"],
        [r"multiple\|escaped\|pipes", "two"],
    ])

    markdown = table.markdown()
    first_data_row, second_data_row = markdown.splitlines()[2:]

    # A field that already uses Markdown's pipe escape is safe as-is.  Turning
    # it into \\\| changes its displayed content (and relies on an odd number
    # of slashes to keep the pipe escaped), rather than preserving the CSV
    # item's intended literal-pipe value.
    assert r"already\|escaped" in first_data_row
    assert r"multiple\|escaped\|pipes" in second_data_row
    assert r"already\\\|escaped" not in first_data_row
    assert r"multiple\\\|escaped\\\|pipes" not in second_data_row

"""Regression tests for artifact-safe charm package names."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib

import pytest
from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("platform", "architecture", "expected_filename"),
    [
        (
            "ubuntu@22.04:amd64",
            "amd64",
            "example-charm_ubuntu@22.04-amd64.charm",
        ),
        (
            "ubuntu@22.04:arm64",
            "arm64",
            "example-charm_ubuntu@22.04-arm64.charm",
        ),
        (
            "amd64",
            "amd64",
            "example-charm_amd64.charm",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_pack_charm_uses_artifact_safe_platform_filename(
    tmp_path: pathlib.Path,
    service_factory,
    platform: str,
    architecture: str,
    expected_filename: str,
):
    """Packed charms must not use colons from multi-base platform labels."""
    project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "example-charm",
            "summary": "An example charm",
            "description": "An example charm used for testing",
            "type": "charm",
            "base": None,
            "build-base": None,
            "platforms": {platform: None},
            "parts": {},
        }
    )
    build_plan = [
        BuildInfo(
            platform=platform,
            build_on=architecture,
            build_for=architecture,
            base=BaseName("ubuntu", "22.04"),
        )
    ]
    package_service = services.PackageService(
        app=APP_METADATA,
        project=project,
        services=service_factory,
        project_dir=tmp_path,
        build_plan=build_plan,
    )

    prime_dir = tmp_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("charm payload")

    packages = package_service.pack(prime_dir, tmp_path)

    expected_path = tmp_path / expected_filename
    assert packages == [expected_path]
    assert expected_path.is_file()
    assert ":" not in expected_path.name
    assert (tmp_path / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt").read_text() == (
        f"{expected_filename}\n"
    )

import pytest

from ucumvert import PintUcumRegistry


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("ucum_code", "expected_unit", "expected_magnitude"),
    [
        ("m[IU]", "international_unit", 1e-3),
        ("k[IU]", "international_unit", 1e3),
        ("m[IU]/L", "international_unit / liter", 1e-3),
        ("k[IU]/L", "international_unit / liter", 1e3),
        # Prefixes on numerator and denominator must be applied independently.
        ("m[IU]/mL", "international_unit / liter", 1.0),
    ],
)
def test_prefix_before_bracketed_international_unit_is_not_a_meter(
    ucum_code, expected_unit, expected_magnitude
):
    """Prefixes attached to [IU] must scale international units, not add meters."""
    ureg = PintUcumRegistry()

    result = ureg.from_ucum(ucum_code).to(expected_unit)

    assert result.magnitude == pytest.approx(expected_magnitude)
    assert str(result.units) == expected_unit

import io

from csv2md.table import Table


def _unescaped_pipe_count(line):
    """Count Markdown table delimiter pipes, ignoring backslash-escaped pipes."""
    count = 0
    for index, char in enumerate(line):
        if char != "|":
            continue

        preceding_backslashes = 0
        cursor = index - 1
        while cursor >= 0 and line[cursor] == "\\":
            preceding_backslashes += 1
            cursor -= 1

        if preceding_backslashes % 2 == 0:
            count += 1

    return count


def _escaped_pipe_representation(value):
    """Accept either documented HTML escaping or Markdown backslash escaping."""
    return value.replace("|", r"\|"), value.replace("|", "|")


def test_markdown_escapes_every_literal_pipe_in_cell_contents():
    cells = [
        ["item", "value"],
        ["|starts-with-pipe", "one"],
        ["ends-with-pipe|", "two"],
        ["contains||consecutive-pipes", "three"],
        ["has|several|pipes", "four"],
    ]

    markdown = Table(cells).markdown()
    data_rows = markdown.splitlines()[2:]

    original_values = [row[0] for row in cells[1:]]
    for line, original_value in zip(data_rows, original_values):
        backslash_escaped, html_escaped = _escaped_pipe_representation(original_value)

        # A two-column Markdown row must only have its opening, separating,
        # and closing table delimiters. Item pipes must not become delimiters.
        assert _unescaped_pipe_count(line) == 3
        assert backslash_escaped in line or html_escaped in line


def test_csv_items_with_existing_pipe_escapes_are_not_double_escaped():
    csv_data = (
        '"a","b"\n'
        '"test|with|pipe|symbol","baz"\n'
        '"test\\|with\\|pipe\\|symbol","baz"\n'
        '"test|with|escaped|pipe","baz"\n'
    )

    markdown = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data)).markdown()
    rows = markdown.splitlines()

    literal_pipe_row = next(line for line in rows if "test" in line and "symbol" in line)
    preescaped_pipe_row = next(line for line in rows if r"test\|with" in line)
    html_escaped_pipe_row = next(line for line in rows if "|" in line)

    # Literal CSV pipes must no longer be interpreted as table separators.
    assert _unescaped_pipe_count(literal_pipe_row) == 3
    assert r"test\|with\|pipe\|symbol" in literal_pipe_row or (
        "test|with|pipe|symbol" in literal_pipe_row
    )

    # Input that is already valid Markdown table escaping must remain escaped
    # once, rather than gaining extra literal backslashes.
    assert r"test\|with\|pipe\|symbol" in preescaped_pipe_row
    assert r"test\\\|with\\\|pipe\\\|symbol" not in preescaped_pipe_row
    assert _unescaped_pipe_count(preescaped_pipe_row) == 3

    # Existing HTML character-code escaping is already safe and should be kept.
    assert "test|with|escaped|pipe" in html_escaped_pipe_row
    assert _unescaped_pipe_count(html_escaped_pipe_row) == 3

"""Regression tests for safe multi-base charm artifact names."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
import zipfile

from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA


def test_pack_multibase_charms_uses_colon_free_artifact_names(
    new_path: pathlib.Path, service_factory
):
    """Multi-base platform labels must not put ':' in packed charm filenames.

    Platform labels use ``:`` to separate a base from its architecture. That is
    valid in the charmcraft.yaml platform key, but not in artifact filenames
    accepted by GitHub Actions.
    """
    project_dir = new_path / "project"
    project_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    prime_dir = new_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("packed payload")
    destination = new_path / "artifacts"
    destination.mkdir()

    platforms = ("ubuntu@22.04:amd64", "ubuntu@22.04:arm64")
    project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "mysql-router-k8s",
            "summary": "A test charm",
            "description": "A test charm",
            "type": "charm",
            "base": None,
            "build-base": None,
            "platforms": {platform: None for platform in platforms},
            "parts": {},
        }
    )

    packages = []
    for platform in platforms:
        architecture = platform.rsplit(":", maxsplit=1)[1]
        package_service = services.PackageService(
            app=APP_METADATA,
            project=project,
            services=service_factory,
            project_dir=project_dir,
            build_plan=[
                BuildInfo(
                    platform=platform,
                    build_on=architecture,
                    build_for=architecture,
                    base=BaseName("ubuntu", "22.04"),
                )
            ],
        )

        packages.extend(package_service.pack(prime_dir, destination))

    expected_names = {
        "mysql-router-k8s_ubuntu@22.04-amd64.charm",
        "mysql-router-k8s_ubuntu@22.04-arm64.charm",
    }

    assert {package.name for package in packages} == expected_names
    assert {path.name for path in destination.iterdir()} == expected_names
    assert all(":" not in package.name for package in packages)

    for package in packages:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(package) as charm_file:
            assert charm_file.namelist() == ["payload.txt"]
            assert charm_file.read("payload.txt") == b"packed payload"

    assert (project_dir / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt").read_text().splitlines() == [
        "mysql-router-k8s_ubuntu@22.04-amd64.charm",
        "mysql-router-k8s_ubuntu@22.04-arm64.charm",
    ]

import io

from csv2md.table import Table


def _single_cell_markdown(value):
    line = Table([[value]]).markdown().splitlines()[0]
    assert line.startswith("| ")
    assert line.endswith(" |")
    return line[2:-2]


def test_escapes_pipes_in_csv_headers_and_data_cells():
    table = Table.parse_csv(
        io.StringIO(
            '"header|pipe","second"\n'
            '"value|with|pipes","plain"\n'
        )
    )

    lines = table.markdown().splitlines()

    # There must still be only two Markdown columns: pipes in item values
    # cannot be emitted as table delimiters.
    assert lines[0].count(" | ") == 1
    assert lines[2].count(" | ") == 1

    assert "header\\|pipe" in lines[0] or "header|pipe" in lines[0]
    assert (
        "value\\|with\\|pipes" in lines[2]
        or "value|with|pipes" in lines[2]
    )


def test_does_not_turn_existing_markdown_pipe_escapes_into_delimiters():
    table = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO('"already\\|escaped\\|pipe"\n'))
    rendered = _single_cell_markdown(table.cells[0][0])

    # The issue's reproduction includes already escaped values.  A second
    # slash before the pipe is incorrect: Markdown consumes the first slash
    # to render the second literally, leaving the pipe to split the table.
    #
    # A correct implementation may retain the valid backslash escapes or
    # normalize them to the documented HTML entity representation.
    assert rendered in (
        r"already\|escaped\|pipe",
        "already|escaped|pipe",
    )
    assert r"already\\|escaped\\|pipe" not in rendered


def test_pipe_after_even_number_of_backslashes_is_escaped():
    value = r"literal\\|pipe"
    rendered = _single_cell_markdown(value)

    # Two preceding slashes do not escape a pipe in Markdown, since they
    # represent one literal slash.  The emitted pipe needs its own escape.
    assert rendered in (
        r"literal\\\|pipe",
        r"literal\\|pipe",
    )


def test_existing_html_pipe_entities_remain_valid_table_content():
    value = "test|with|escaped|pipe"

    # HTML entities are explicitly recommended by the issue and should not
    # be damaged or have a literal pipe delimiter introduced.
    assert _single_cell_markdown(value) == value


def test_escaped_values_do_not_break_aligned_tables_with_generated_headers():
    markdown = Table(
        [
            ["left|value", "right|value"],
            ["another|left", "another|right"],
        ]
    ).markdown(
        center_aligned_columns=[0],
        right_aligned_columns=[1],
        no_header_row=True,
    )

    lines = markdown.splitlines()

    # Default headers, separator, and both data rows must remain two-column
    # Markdown rows even when their values contain pipes.
    for line in (lines[0], lines[1], lines[2], lines[3]):
        assert line.count(" | ") == 1

    assert "left\\|value" in lines[2] or "left|value" in lines[2]
    assert "right\\|value" in lines[2] or "right|value" in lines[2]
    assert lines[1].startswith("| :")
    assert lines[1].endswith(": |")

import pathlib

import pytest
from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA


@pytest.mark.parametrize("architecture", ["amd64", "arm64"])
def test_pack_multibase_charm_uses_artifact_safe_filename(
    tmp_path: pathlib.Path, service_factory, architecture: str
):
    """Multi-base platform labels must not leave ':' in packed artifact names.

    A colon is part of the platform shorthand syntax, but is not accepted in
    GitHub Actions artifact or release filenames.  Verify the actual packed
    artifact and the output-package tracking file both use the safe name.
    """
    platform = f"ubuntu@22.04:{architecture}"
    project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "multi-base-charm",
            "summary": "A test charm",
            "description": "A test charm with a multi-base platform label",
            "type": "charm",
            "platforms": {platform: None},
            "parts": {},
        }
    )
    build_plan = [
        BuildInfo(
            platform=platform,
            build_on=architecture,
            build_for=architecture,
            base=BaseName("ubuntu", "22.04"),
        )
    ]
    package_service = services.PackageService(
        app=APP_METADATA,
        project=project,
        services=service_factory,
        project_dir=tmp_path,
        build_plan=build_plan,
    )

    prime_dir = tmp_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("charm payload")

    packages = package_service.pack(prime_dir, tmp_path)

    assert len(packages) == 1
    package = packages[0]
    assert package.exists()
    assert package.suffix == ".charm"

    # The platform still identifies the base and target architecture, while
    # removing the character rejected by GitHub artifact/release uploads.
    assert "ubuntu" in package.name
    assert "22.04" in package.name
    assert architecture in package.name
    assert ":" not in package.name
    assert ":" not in str(package)

    recorded_packages = (
        tmp_path / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt"
    ).read_text().splitlines()
    assert recorded_packages == [package.name]
    assert all(":" not in name for name in recorded_packages)

import io

from csv2md.table import Table


def _unescaped_pipes(line):
    """Return pipes that Markdown interprets as table delimiters."""
    pipes = []
    for index, character in enumerate(line):
        if character != "|":
            continue

        backslashes = 0
        cursor = index - 1
        while cursor >= 0 and line[cursor] == "\\":
            backslashes += 1
            cursor -= 1

        if backslashes % 2 == 0:
            pipes.append(index)
    return pipes


def test_markdown_escapes_pipes_in_quoted_csv_headers_and_items():
    table = Table.parse_csv(
        io.StringIO(
            '"column|name",other\n'
            '"value|with|pipes",plain\n'
        )
    )

    lines = table.markdown().splitlines()

    # A two-column Markdown table has only a leading, separating, and
    # trailing structural pipe. Cell contents must not add delimiters.
    assert all(len(_unescaped_pipes(line)) == 3 for line in lines)

    # Both a backslash escape and the HTML entity recommended by the issue
    # are valid Markdown-safe representations.
    assert "column\\|name" in lines[0] or "column|name" in lines[0]
    assert (
        "value\\|with\\|pipes" in lines[2]
        or "value|with|pipes" in lines[2]
    )


def test_markdown_does_not_double_escape_preescaped_pipes():
    table = Table.parse_csv(
        io.StringIO(
            "name,value\n"
            '"already\\|escaped|and|new",ok\n'
        )
    )

    data_row = table.markdown().splitlines()[2]

    # The issue explicitly includes cells that already contain Markdown's
    # pipe escape. Turning \| into \\| makes Markdown parse the pipe as a
    # table delimiter, so all pipes in this cell must remain safe.
    assert len(_unescaped_pipes(data_row)) == 3

    # The formerly raw pipes must also be escaped.
    assert "and\\|new" in data_row or "and|new" in data_row


def test_pipe_escaping_works_with_alignment_and_generated_headers():
    table = Table.parse_csv(
        io.StringIO(
            '"left|value",123\n'
            '"another|value",456\n'
        )
    )

    lines = table.markdown(
        center_aligned_columns=[0],
        right_aligned_columns=[1],
        no_header_row=True,
    ).splitlines()

    # Escaping data must not be skipped by alternate table formatting modes.
    assert all(len(_unescaped_pipes(line)) == 3 for line in lines)
    assert "left\\|value" in lines[2] or "left|value" in lines[2]
    assert "another\\|value" in lines[3] or "another|value" in lines[3]

    separator_columns = [part.strip() for part in lines[1].split("|")[1:-1]]
    assert separator_columns[0].startswith(":")
    assert separator_columns[0].endswith(":")
    assert separator_columns[1].endswith(":")

    return services.PackageService(
        app=APP_METADATA,
        project=simple_charm,
        services=service_factory,
        project_dir=new_path,

    )


def test_pack_multi_base_charms_creates_colon_free_distinct_artifacts(
    new_path: pathlib.Path, package_service
):
    """Packed multi-base artifacts must be suitable for GitHub uploads.

    Platform labels use ':' to separate the base and architecture.  The label
    must not be used verbatim in the artifact filename, while builds for
    different architectures must still produce distinct artifacts.
    """
    platforms = ("ubuntu@22.04:amd64", "ubuntu@22.04:arm64")
    package_service._project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "mysql-router-k8s",
            "description": "",
            "summary": "",
            "type": "charm",
            "base": None,
            "platforms": {platform: None for platform in platforms},
            "parts": {},
        }
    )

    prime_dir = new_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "dispatch").write_text("#!/bin/sh\n")

    destination = new_path / "artifacts"
    destination.mkdir()

    packages = []
    for platform in platforms:
        # Normal multi-platform packing creates one PackageService per build
        # plan. Select each platform as those independent builds would.
        package_service._platform = platform
        packages.extend(package_service.pack(prime_dir, destination))

    artifact_names = [package.name for package in packages]

    assert len(artifact_names) == 2
    assert len(set(artifact_names)) == 2
    assert all(name.endswith(".charm") for name in artifact_names)
    assert all(":" not in name for name in artifact_names)
    assert any("amd64" in name for name in artifact_names)
    assert any("arm64" in name for name in artifact_names)
    assert all(package.is_file() for package in packages)

    # Consumers such as CI workflows obtain artifact names through this file,
    # so it must report the same uploadable names.
    output_file = package_service.project_dir / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt"
    assert output_file.read_text().splitlines() == artifact_names

import io

from csv2md.table import Table


def test_markdown_escapes_pipes_from_quoted_csv_cells_in_headers_and_values():
    table = Table.parse_csv(
        io.StringIO(
            '"h|i",b\n'
            '"x|y","p|q"\n'
            '"|","|||"\n'
        )
    )

    assert table.markdown() == (
        '| h\\|i | b      |\n'
        '| ---- | ------ |\n'
        '| x\\|y | p\\|q   |\n'
        '| \\|   | \\|\\|\\| |'
    )


def test_markdown_keeps_html_pipe_entities_and_uses_escaped_widths_for_alignment():
    table = Table(
        [
            ['a|b', 'number'],
            ['x', '7'],
            ['entity', 'a|b'],
        ]
    )

    assert table.markdown(right_aligned_columns=[1]) == (
        '| a\\|b   | number   |\n'
        '| ------ | -------: |\n'
        '| x      | 7        |\n'
        '| entity | a|b |'
    )


def test_markdown_escapes_pipes_when_default_headers_are_generated():
    table = Table([['a|b', 'c']])

    assert table.markdown(no_header_row=True) == (
        '| a    | b |\n'
        '| ---- | - |\n'
        '| a\\|b | c |'
    )

"""Regression tests for safe multi-base charm artifact filenames."""

import pathlib
import zipfile

import pytest
from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "selected_platform",
    [
        "ubuntu@22.04:amd64",
        "ubuntu@22.04:arm64",
    ],
)
def test_pack_multibase_charm_uses_artifact_filename_without_colon(
    new_path: pathlib.Path,
    service_factory,
    selected_platform: str,
):
    """Multi-base platform labels must not create colon-containing charm files."""
    project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "multi-base-charm",
            "summary": "A multi-base charm",
            "description": "A charm built for more than one Ubuntu architecture.",
            "type": "charm",
            "platforms": {
                "ubuntu@22.04:amd64": None,
                "ubuntu@22.04:arm64": None,
            },
            "parts": {},
        }
    )
    architecture = selected_platform.rsplit(":", maxsplit=1)[1]
    build_plan = [
        BuildInfo(
            platform=selected_platform,
            build_on=architecture,
            build_for=architecture,
            base=BaseName("ubuntu", "22.04"),
        )
    ]

    package_service = services.PackageService(
        app=APP_METADATA,
        project=project,
        services=service_factory,
        project_dir=new_path,
        build_plan=build_plan,
    )

    prime_dir = new_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("charm payload")

    artifact_dir = new_path / "artifacts"
    artifact_dir.mkdir()
    packages = package_service.pack(prime_dir, artifact_dir)

    assert len(packages) == 1
    charm_path = packages[0]

    # GitHub Actions artifacts and releases reject ':' in artifact filenames.
    assert ":" not in charm_path.name
    assert charm_path.suffix == ".charm"

    # Sanitising the filename must not lose the meaningful base or architecture.
    assert "ubuntu@22.04" in charm_path.name
    assert architecture in charm_path.name

    assert charm_path.is_file()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(charm_path) as charm_archive:
        assert charm_archive.read("payload.txt") == b"charm payload"

    # The path communicated to subsequent Charmcraft/CI steps must be the
    # sanitized artifact name as well.
    output_packages = new_path / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt"
    assert output_packages.read_text().splitlines() == [charm_path.name]
    assert ":" not in output_packages.read_text()
