import add_trailing_comma


def _assert_fixed_in_one_pass(tmp_path, source, expected):
    filename = tmp_path / 'example.py'
    filename.write_text(source, encoding='UTF-8')

    assert add_trailing_comma.main([str(filename)]) == 1
    assert filename.read_text(encoding='UTF-8') == expected

    # A second run must not be needed to add the trailing comma.
    assert add_trailing_comma.main([str(filename)]) == 0
    assert filename.read_text(encoding='UTF-8') == expected


def test_multiline_implicitly_concatenated_call_argument_gets_comma_in_one_pass(
        tmp_path,
):
    _assert_fixed_in_one_pass(
        tmp_path,
        "f('long'\n"
        "  'literal')\n",
        "f(\n"
        "    'long'\n"
        "    'literal',\n"
        ")\n",
    )


def test_multiline_string_argument_of_expression_callee_gets_comma_in_one_pass(
        tmp_path,
):
    # The callable does not have to be a bare name; this remains a function
    # call with a single, implicitly concatenated multiline string argument.
    _assert_fixed_in_one_pass(
        tmp_path,
        "get_callback()('long'\n"
        "  'literal')\n",
        "get_callback()(\n"
        "    'long'\n"
        "    'literal',\n"
        ")\n",
    )


def test_multiline_string_argument_of_subscript_callee_gets_comma_in_one_pass(
        tmp_path,
):
    _assert_fixed_in_one_pass(
        tmp_path,
        "callbacks[0]('long'\n"
        "  'literal')\n",
        "callbacks[0](\n"
        "    'long'\n"
        "    'literal',\n"
        ")\n",
    )


def test_multiline_implicit_string_concatenation_outside_a_call_stays_a_string(
        tmp_path,
):
    # A comma is only needed for the call argument.  Adding one here would
    # change the parenthesized string expression into a tuple.

        tmp_path,
        "value = ('long'\n"
        "  'literal')\n",
        "value = (\n"
        "    'long'\n"
        "    'literal'\n"
        ")\n",
    )

"""Regression tests for handling suspect and corrupt file copies."""

from unittest.mock import patch

from alpenhorn.daemon.update import UpdateableNode
from alpenhorn.db import (
    ArchiveAcq,
    ArchiveFile,
    ArchiveFileCopy,
    StorageGroup,
    StorageNode,
)


def test_daemon_deletes_released_suspect_and_corrupt_copies(
    queue,
    simplenode,
    simpleacq,
    archivefile,
    archivefilecopy,
):
    """The daemon deletes X/N and M/N copies, not just healthy Y/N copies."""
    unode = UpdateableNode(queue, simplenode)

    suspect = archivefilecopy(
        node=simplenode,
        file=archivefile(name="suspect", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="X",
        wants_file="N",
    )
    corrupt = archivefilecopy(
        node=simplenode,
        file=archivefile(name="corrupt", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="N",
    )
    wanted_corrupt = archivefilecopy(
        node=simplenode,
        file=archivefile(name="wanted-corrupt", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="Y",
    )

    with patch.object(unode.io, "delete") as delete:
        unode.update_delete()

    deleted_ids = {
        copy.id
        for delete_call in delete.call_args_list
        for copy in delete_call.args[0]
    }

    assert suspect.id in deleted_ids
    assert corrupt.id in deleted_ids
    assert wanted_corrupt.id not in deleted_ids


def test_daemon_checks_wanted_corrupt_copies_but_not_released_ones(
    queue,
    simplenode,
    simpleacq,
    archivefile,
    archivefilecopy,
):
    """M/N copies are headed for deletion and must not receive integrity checks."""
    unode = UpdateableNode(queue, simplenode)

    released_corrupt = archivefilecopy(
        node=simplenode,
        file=archivefile(name="released-corrupt", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="N",
    )
    wanted_corrupt = archivefilecopy(
        node=simplenode,
        file=archivefile(name="wanted-corrupt", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="Y",
    )
    deferred_corrupt = archivefilecopy(
        node=simplenode,
        file=archivefile(name="deferred-corrupt", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="M",
    )

    with patch.object(unode.io, "before_update", return_value=True), patch.object(
        unode.io, "check"
    ) as check, patch.object(unode, "update_free_space"), patch.object(
        unode, "update_delete"
    ), patch(
        "alpenhorn.daemon.update.auto_import.update_observer"
    ), patch(
        "alpenhorn.daemon.update.RemoteNode"
    ):
        unode.update()

    checked_ids = {check_call.args[0].id for check_call in check.call_args_list}

    assert released_corrupt.id not in checked_ids
    assert checked_ids == {wanted_corrupt.id, deferred_corrupt.id}


def test_node_clean_include_bad_marks_suspect_and_corrupt_copies(clidb, cli):
    """The --include-bad option selects X/M copies while normal clean does not."""
    group = StorageGroup.create(name="group")
    node = StorageNode.create(name="node", group=group, storage_type="F")
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="acq")

    healthy = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node,
        file=ArchiveFile.create(name="healthy", acq=acq, size_b=1),
        has_file="Y",
        wants_file="Y",
    )
    suspect = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node,
        file=ArchiveFile.create(name="suspect", acq=acq, size_b=1),
        has_file="X",
        wants_file="Y",
    )
    corrupt = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node,
        file=ArchiveFile.create(name="corrupt", acq=acq, size_b=1),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="Y",
    )

    # The option is opt-in: ordinary cleaning retains its historical behaviour.
    cli(0, ["node", "clean", node.name, "--force"])
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(healthy.id).wants_file == "M"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(suspect.id).wants_file == "Y"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(corrupt.id).wants_file == "Y"

    cli(0, ["node", "clean", node.name, "--force", "--include-bad"])
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(suspect.id).wants_file == "M"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(corrupt.id).wants_file == "M"

import pytest

from parsel import Selector


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("encoding", "body", "expected"),
    [
        ("b'utf8'", b"<html><head><title>Caf\xc3\xa9</title></head></html>", "Café"),
        (
            "b'iso-8859-1'",
            b"<html><head><title>Ol\xe1</title></head></html>",
            "Olá",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_css_works_when_html_encoding_is_a_bytes_repr(encoding, body, expected):
    """A bytes representation of a valid encoding must be accepted by lxml."""
    response = Selector(body=body, type="html", encoding=encoding)

    assert response.css("title::text").get() == expected
    assert response.xpath("//title/text()").get() == expected


def test_css_works_when_xml_encoding_is_a_bytes_repr():
    """The encoding normalization applies to XML parsers as well as HTML parsers."""
    response = Selector(
        body=b"<document><title>Caf\xc3\xa9</title></document>",
        type="xml",
        encoding="b'utf8'",
    )

    assert response.css("title::text").get() == "Café"


def test_invalid_bytes_repr_encoding_still_raises_lookup_error():
    """Only representations of real codecs should be normalized."""
    with pytest.raises(LookupError):
        Selector(
            body=b"<html><head><title>Example</title></head></html>",
            type="html",
            encoding="b'not-a-real-encoding'",
        )

import pytest

from parsel import Selector


STRINGIFIED_UTF8_BYTES = str(b"utf8")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("selector_type", [None, "html", "xml"])
def test_stringified_bytes_encoding_parses_markup_for_css(selector_type):
    """An encoding accidentally converted with str(bytes) must still be usable."""
    selector = Selector(
        body="<html><head><title>Parsel café</title></head></html>".encode("utf8"),
        type=selector_type,
        encoding=STRINGIFIED_UTF8_BYTES,
    )

    assert selector.css("title::text").get() == "Parsel café"


def test_stringified_bytes_encoding_works_for_text_body():
    """The encoding must be normalized before decoding text selector bodies."""
    selector = Selector(
        body="Parsel café".encode("utf8"),
        type="text",
        encoding=STRINGIFIED_UTF8_BYTES,
    )

    assert selector.get() == "Parsel café"


def test_stringified_bytes_utf8_encoding_keeps_json_autodetection():
    """A stringified utf8 bytes encoding must behave exactly like ``utf8``."""
    selector = Selector(
        body=b'{"title": "Parsel"}',
        encoding=STRINGIFIED_UTF8_BYTES,
    )

    assert selector.type == "json"
    assert selector.jmespath("title").get() == "Parsel"

            "factory()(\n"

            "callbacks['default']('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "callbacks['default'](\n"
            "    'long'\n"

            ")",

            "f('long'  # continued literal\n"
            "  'literal')",

            "    'long'  # continued literal\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",

import pytest

from add_trailing_comma import _fix_src


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('src', 'expected'),
    (
        (
            "f('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "f(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        (
            "f('one'\n"
            "  'two'\n"
            "  'three')",
            "f(\n"
            "    'one'\n"
            "    'two'\n"
            "    'three',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        # A call expression is not necessarily preceded directly by NAME.
        # This is the same type of call argument and must be fixed in one pass.
        (
            "factory()('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "factory()(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
    ),
)
def test_multiline_implicitly_concatenated_call_strings_fixed_in_one_pass(
        src, expected,
):
    result = _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False)

    assert result == expected
    assert _fix_src(result, py35_plus=False) == result


def test_multiline_implicitly_concatenated_strings_in_condition_are_not_a_call():
    """Only calls get trailing commas; parenthesized expressions do not."""
    src = (
        "if ('long'\n"
        "    'literal'):\n"
        "    pass"
    )
    expected = (
        "if (\n"
        "    'long'\n"
        "    'literal'\n"
        "):\n"
        "    pass"
    )

    assert _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False) == expected

import pytest

import add_trailing_comma


def _assert_fixed_in_one_pass(tmp_path, source, expected):
    filename = tmp_path / 'example.py'
    filename.write_text(source, encoding='UTF-8')

    # The initial rewrite must both expand the call and add its trailing comma.
    assert add_trailing_comma.main([str(filename)]) == 1
    assert filename.read_text(encoding='UTF-8') == expected

    # No second invocation should be required to add the comma.
    assert add_trailing_comma.main([str(filename)]) == 0
    assert filename.read_text(encoding='UTF-8') == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('source', 'expected'),
    (
        pytest.param(
            "f('long'\n"
            "  'literal')\n",
            "f(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")\n",
            id='bare-function',
        ),
        pytest.param(
            "f('first'\n"
            "  'second'\n"
            "  'third')\n",
            "f(\n"
            "    'first'\n"
            "    'second'\n"
            "    'third',\n"
            ")\n",
            id='more-than-two-implicitly-concatenated-strings',
        ),
        # A subscript expression is callable too; its final token before the
        # call paren is ']', rather than a NAME.
        pytest.param(
            "handlers['long_name']('long'\n"
            "                      'literal')\n",
            "handlers['long_name'](\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")\n",
            id='subscripted-callable',
        ),
        # Likewise, the result of a call may itself be called.
        pytest.param(
            "factory()('long'\n"
            "          'literal')\n",
            "factory()(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")\n",
            id='called-result',
        ),
    ),
)
def test_multiline_implicit_string_call_is_fully_fixed_in_one_pass(
        tmp_path, source, expected,
):
    _assert_fixed_in_one_pass(tmp_path, source, expected)

"""Regression tests for the default encoding used when building selectors."""

import json

from parsel import Selector
import parsel.selector as selector_module


def test_default_encoding_uses_utf8_hyphenated_name_with_html_parser(monkeypatch):
    """Default parsing must work on lxml builds which reject the ``utf8`` alias.

    This models the reported Windows/lxml behavior while exercising Selector's
    public text, body, and lazy ``type="text"`` parsing paths.
    """
    real_parser_cls = selector_module._ctgroup["html"]["_parser"]
    seen_encodings = []

    def parser_rejecting_utf8_alias(*args, **kwargs):
        encoding = kwargs.get("encoding")
        seen_encodings.append(encoding)
        if encoding == "utf8":
            raise LookupError("unknown encoding: 'b'utf8''")
        return real_parser_cls(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setitem(
        selector_module._ctgroup["html"], "_parser", parser_rejecting_utf8_alias
    )

    html = "<html><head><title>café</title></head><body></body></html>"

    # This is the tutorial-style usage from the report.
    assert Selector(text=html).css("title::text").get() == "café"

    # Bytes input must receive the same safe default.
    assert Selector(body=html.encode("utf-8")).css("title::text").get() == "café"

    # ``type='text'`` delays HTML parsing until CSS/XPath is used, and must not
    # reintroduce the old alias through Selector._get_root.
    assert (
        Selector(text="<title>lazy café</title>", type="text")
        .css("title::text")
        .get()
        == "lazy café"
    )

    assert seen_encodings == ["utf-8", "utf-8", "utf-8"]


def test_default_utf8_hyphenated_encoding_keeps_json_bytes_detection():
    """Changing the default must not cause UTF-8 JSON bytes to become HTML."""
    body = json.dumps({"title": "café"}, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")

    selector = Selector(body=body)

    assert selector.type == "json"
    assert selector.jmespath("title").get() == "café"

"""Regression tests for the default encoding used by HTML selectors."""

from parsel import Selector
from parsel import selector as selector_module


def test_default_html_encoding_is_windows_lxml_compatible(monkeypatch):
    """Default selector parsing must use the canonical ``utf-8`` spelling.

    Some lxml builds reject the historical ``utf8`` default.  Replace the
    parser with a platform-like wrapper that accepts only the portable spelling,
    while exercising Selector through its public text/body/CSS APIs.
    """
    original_parser = selector_module._ctgroup["html"]["_parser"]
    parser_encodings = []

    def windows_compatible_html_parser(*args, **kwargs):
        encoding = kwargs.get("encoding")
        parser_encodings.append(encoding)
        if encoding != "utf-8":
            raise LookupError(f"unknown encoding: {encoding!r}")
        return original_parser(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setitem(
        selector_module._ctgroup["html"],
        "_parser",
        windows_compatible_html_parser,
    )

    assert Selector(text="<html><title>text input</title></html>").css(
        "title::text"
    ).get() == "text input"

    assert Selector(body=b"<html><title>bytes input</title></html>").css(
        "title::text"
    ).get() == "bytes input"

    # Text selectors parse lazily when CSS/XPath is used, through _get_root().
    assert Selector(text="<title>lazy input</title>", type="text").css(
        "title::text"
    ).get() == "lazy input"

    # The non-huge-tree parser path must use the same safe default.
    assert Selector(
        text="<html><title>non huge tree</title></html>",
        huge_tree=False,
    ).css("title::text").get() == "non huge tree"

    assert parser_encodings
    assert set(parser_encodings) == {"utf-8"}

from __future__ import absolute_import
from __future__ import unicode_literals

import pytest

from add_trailing_comma import _fix_src


def test_implicit_multiline_string_argument_gets_comma_on_first_pass():
    src = (
        "f('long'\n"
        "  'literal')"
    )
    expected = (
        "f(\n"
        "    'long'\n"
        "    'literal',\n"
        ")"
    )

    fixed = _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False)
    assert fixed == expected
    assert _fix_src(fixed, py35_plus=False) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('src', 'expected'),
    (
        # A call target need not be a bare name.  These calls have the same
        # implicitly-concatenated-string AST positioning issue as f(...).
        (
            "factory()('long'\n"
            "          'literal')",
            "factory()(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        (
            "callbacks[0]('long'\n"
            "             'literal')",
            "callbacks[0](\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
    ),
)
def test_implicit_multiline_string_argument_for_any_call_target_is_one_pass(
        src,
        expected,
):
    fixed = _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False)

    assert fixed == expected
    assert _fix_src(fixed, py35_plus=False) == expected

import pytest
from lxml import html

from parsel import Selector
from parsel import selector as selector_module


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "selector_kwargs",
    [
        {"text": "<html><head><title>Café</title></head></html>"},
        {"body": b"<html><head><title>Caf\xc3\xa9</title></head></html>"},
    ],
    ids=["text-input", "bytes-input"],
)
def test_default_html_encoding_is_accepted_by_lxml_builds_rejecting_utf8_alias(
    monkeypatch, selector_kwargs
):
    """Default HTML selectors must use lxml's portable ``utf-8`` spelling.

    The reported Windows lxml build rejects ``utf8`` when it is supplied as
    the parser encoding.  Replace the HTML parser with an equivalent strict
    wrapper to exercise that platform-specific behavior on every platform.
    """
    real_html_parser = html.HTMLParser

    def strict_html_parser(*args, **kwargs):
        if kwargs.get("encoding") != "utf-8":
            raise LookupError(f"unknown encoding: {kwargs.get('encoding')!r}")
        return real_html_parser(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setitem(
        selector_module._ctgroup["html"], "_parser", strict_html_parser
    )

    response = Selector(**selector_kwargs)

    # This is the tutorial-style operation from the report.  Selector creation
    # and CSS selection must both succeed.
    assert response.css("title::text").get() == "Café"


def test_default_bytes_encoding_keeps_json_auto_detection():
    """Changing the default spelling must not stop JSON bytes from being JSON."""
    response = Selector(body=b'{"title": "Example"}')

    assert response.type == "json"
    assert response.jmespath("title").get() == "Example"

import inspect

from gspread.utils import (
    DateTimeOption,
    Dimension,
    ValueInputOption,
    ValueRenderOption,
)
from gspread.worksheet import Worksheet


class RecordingClient:
    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = []

    def values_get(self, spreadsheet_id, range_name, params=None):
        self.calls.append(
            ("values_get", spreadsheet_id, range_name, params if params is not None else {})
        )
        return {
            "range": range_name,
            "majorDimension": "ROWS",
            "values": [["value"]],
        }

    def values_batch_get(self, spreadsheet_id, ranges, params=None):
        self.calls.append(
            (
                "values_batch_get",
                spreadsheet_id,
                ranges,
                params if params is not None else {},
            )
        )
        return {
            "valueRanges": [
                {"range": range_name, "majorDimension": "ROWS", "values": []}
                for range_name in ranges
            ]
        }

    def values_update(self, spreadsheet_id, range_name, params=None, body=None):
        self.calls.append(("values_update", spreadsheet_id, range_name, params, body))
        return {"updatedRange": range_name}

    def values_batch_update(self, spreadsheet_id, body=None):
        self.calls.append(("values_batch_update", spreadsheet_id, body))
        return {"totalUpdatedCells": 1}


def make_worksheet():
    return Worksheet(
        "spreadsheet-id",
        RecordingClient(),
        {
            "sheetId": 123,
            "title": "Sheet 1",
            "index": 0,
            "gridProperties": {"rowCount": 100, "columnCount": 26},
        },
    )

import pytest

import jwt
from jwt.exceptions import MissingRequiredClaimError


def test_decode_ignores_null_audience_when_no_audience_is_requested():
    token = jwt.encode(
        {"sub": "example", "aud": None},
        "secret",
        algorithm="HS256",
    )

    assert jwt.decode(token, "secret", algorithms=["HS256"]) == {
        "sub": "example",
        "aud": None,
    }


def test_null_audience_is_missing_when_an_audience_is_requested():
    """aud: null must validate identically to an omitted aud claim."""
    token = jwt.encode(
        {"sub": "example", "aud": None},
        "secret",
        algorithm="HS256",
    )

    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc:
        jwt.decode(
            token,
            "secret",
            algorithms=["HS256"],
            audience="urn:expected-audience",
        )

    assert exc.value.claim == "aud"

import textwrap

from checkov.cloudformation.runner import Runner
from checkov.runner_filter import RunnerFilter


def _run_cloudformation(tmp_path, content, checks):
    template = tmp_path / "template.yaml"
    template.write_text(textwrap.dedent(content))
    return Runner().run(
        root_folder=None,
        files=[str(template)],
        runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=checks),
    )


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_suppresses_issue_example_without_reason(tmp_path):
    """The exact `#checkov:skip=<id>:` syntax from the issue must suppress CFN checks."""
    report = _run_cloudformation(
        tmp_path,
        """
        AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
        Parameters:
          VpcId:
            Type: String
          SSHLocation:
            Type: String
            Default: 0.0.0.0/0
        Resources:
          #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:
          SecurityGroup:
            Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
            Properties:
              GroupDescription: Folding@home spot instance security group
              VpcId: !Ref VpcId
              SecurityGroupIngress:
                - IpProtocol: tcp
                  FromPort: 22
                  ToPort: 22
                  CidrIp: !Ref SSHLocation
        """,
        checks=["CKV_AWS_24"],
    )

    assert not report.failed_checks
    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].resource == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SecurityGroup"


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_suppresses_only_the_annotated_resource(tmp_path):
    report = _run_cloudformation(
        tmp_path,
        """
        AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
        Resources:
          #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: SSH access is intentionally public
          SuppressedSecurityGroup:
            Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
            Properties:
              GroupDescription: public ssh is accepted for this test
              SecurityGroupIngress:
                - IpProtocol: tcp
                  FromPort: 22
                  ToPort: 22
                  CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0

          UnsuppressedSecurityGroup:
            Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
            Properties:
              GroupDescription: this resource must still be checked
              SecurityGroupIngress:
                - IpProtocol: tcp
                  FromPort: 22
                  ToPort: 22
                  CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
        """,
        checks=["CKV_AWS_24"],
    )

    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1

    skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
    assert skipped.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert skipped.resource == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SuppressedSecurityGroup"
    assert skipped.check_result["suppress_comment"] == " SSH access is intentionally public"

    assert report.failed_checks[0].resource == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.UnsuppressedSecurityGroup"


def test_cloudformation_adjacent_skip_comments_for_multiple_checks_are_all_honored(tmp_path):
    """Every adjacent skip annotation must be supplied to the resource scan."""
    report = _run_cloudformation(
        tmp_path,
        """
        AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
        Resources:
          #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: public SSH is required
          #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_23: public RDP is required
          SecurityGroup:
            Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
            Properties:
              GroupDescription: intentionally public management ports
              SecurityGroupIngress:
                - IpProtocol: tcp
                  FromPort: 22
                  ToPort: 22
                  CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
                - IpProtocol: tcp
                  FromPort: 3389
                  ToPort: 3389
                  CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
        """,
        checks=["CKV_AWS_24", "CKV_AWS_23"],
    )

    assert not report.failed_checks
    assert {record.check_id for record in report.skipped_checks} == {
        "CKV_AWS_24",
        "CKV_AWS_23",
    }
    assert {record.resource for record in report.skipped_checks} == {
        "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SecurityGroup"
    }

    skipped = {record.check_id: record for record in report.skipped_checks}
    assert skipped["CKV_AWS_24"].check_result["suppress_comment"] == " public SSH is required"
    assert skipped["CKV_AWS_23"].check_result["suppress_comment"] == " public RDP is required"


def test_cloudformation_skip_comments_do_not_cross_resource_boundaries(tmp_path):
    """An annotation above one resource must not suppress a later resource."""
    report = _run_cloudformation(
        tmp_path,
        """
        AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
        Resources:
          #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: exception applies only to the first group
          FirstSecurityGroup:
            Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
            Properties:
              GroupDescription: first group
              SecurityGroupIngress:
                - IpProtocol: tcp
                  FromPort: 22
                  ToPort: 22
                  CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0

          SecondSecurityGroup:
            Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
            Properties:
              GroupDescription: second group
              SecurityGroupIngress:
                - IpProtocol: tcp
                  FromPort: 22
                  ToPort: 22
                  CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
        """,
        checks=["CKV_AWS_24"],
    )

    assert {record.resource for record in report.skipped_checks} == {
        "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.FirstSecurityGroup"
    }
    assert {record.resource for record in report.failed_checks} == {
        "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SecondSecurityGroup"
    }

import pytest

from add_trailing_comma import _fix_src


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('src', 'expected'),
    (
        # The reported regression: adjacent string tokens are one AST argument,
        # but span lines and must receive their trailing comma on the first run.
        (
            "f('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "f(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        # The callable may be produced by another call.  Ordinary multiline
        # calls of this form are already supported and implicit string
        # concatenation must not make this case require a second pass.
        (
            "factory()('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "factory()(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        # Subscription is another valid callable expression, where the token
        # immediately before the argument parenthesis is not a NAME.
        (
            "callbacks[0]('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "callbacks[0](\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        # Parenthesizing a callable must not affect trailing-comma behavior.
        (
            "(f)('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "(f)(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
    ),
)
def test_multiline_implicitly_concatenated_call_argument_fixed_in_one_pass(
        src, expected,
):
    ret = _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False)

    assert ret == expected
    # This is the regression condition: a second run must be a no-op rather
    # than the run that finally inserts the comma.
    assert _fix_src(ret, py35_plus=False) == expected


def test_multiline_implicitly_concatenated_call_argument_with_comment():
    src = (
        "f('long'  # still part of the implicit concatenation\n"
        "  'literal')"
    )
    expected = (
        "f(\n"
        "    'long'  # still part of the implicit concatenation\n"
        "    'literal',\n"
        ")"
    )

    assert _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False) == expected

import pytest

import jwt
from jwt.exceptions import InvalidAudienceError, MissingRequiredClaimError


def test_null_audience_is_accepted_when_no_audience_is_requested():
    payload = {"sub": "example-user", "aud": None}
    token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret", algorithm="HS256")

    assert jwt.decode(token, "secret", algorithms=["HS256"]) == payload


def test_null_audience_is_treated_as_absent_when_an_audience_is_requested():
    """Ignoring aud=null must match the behavior of a token with no aud claim."""
    token = jwt.encode(
        {"sub": "example-user", "aud": None},
        "secret",
        algorithm="HS256",
    )

    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc:
        jwt.decode(
            token,
            "secret",
            algorithms=["HS256"],
            audience="urn:expected-audience",
        )

    assert exc.value.claim == "aud"


def test_absent_audience_requires_a_claim_when_an_audience_is_requested():
    token = jwt.encode({"sub": "example-user"}, "secret", algorithm="HS256")

    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc:
        jwt.decode(
            token,
            "secret",
            algorithms=["HS256"],
            audience="urn:expected-audience",
        )

    assert exc.value.claim == "aud"


def test_non_null_audience_is_not_ignored_when_no_audience_is_requested():
    token = jwt.encode(
        {"sub": "example-user", "aud": "urn:token-audience"},
        "secret",
        algorithm="HS256",
    )

    with pytest.raises(InvalidAudienceError):
        jwt.decode(token, "secret", algorithms=["HS256"])

from checkov.cloudformation.runner import Runner
from checkov.runner_filter import RunnerFilter


def _security_group(name):
    return f"""\
  {name}:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: test security group
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
"""


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_suppresses_only_annotated_resource(tmp_path):
    template = """\
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: SSH access is intentional
""" + _security_group("AnnotatedGroup") + _security_group("UnannotatedGroup")

    template_path = tmp_path / "security_groups.yaml"
    template_path.write_text(template)

    report = Runner().run(
        root_folder=None,
        files=[str(template_path)],
        runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=["CKV_AWS_24"]),
    )

    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1

    skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
    failed = report.failed_checks[0]
    assert skipped.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert skipped.resource == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.AnnotatedGroup"
    assert skipped.check_result["suppress_comment"] == " SSH access is intentional"

    assert failed.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert failed.resource == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.UnannotatedGroup"


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_with_empty_reason_is_honored(tmp_path):
    # This is the syntax from the reported CloudFormation example: the colon is
    # present but no human-readable reason follows it.
    template = """\
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:
""" + _security_group("SecurityGroup")

    template_path = tmp_path / "suppressed_security_group.yaml"
    template_path.write_text(template)

    report = Runner().run(
        root_folder=str(tmp_path),
        runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=["CKV_AWS_24"]),
    )

    assert not report.failed_checks
    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].resource == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SecurityGroup"

import jwt
from jwt.exceptions import MissingRequiredClaimError


SECRET = "secret"


def _token(payload):
    return jwt.encode(payload, SECRET, algorithm="HS256")


def test_null_audience_is_accepted_when_no_audience_is_requested():
    payload = {"sub": "user-123", "aud": None}

    decoded = jwt.decode(_token(payload), SECRET, algorithms=["HS256"])

    # Validation ignores the null claim, while decoding preserves the claim.
    assert decoded == payload


def test_null_audience_behaves_like_absent_audience_when_audience_is_requested():
    requested_audience = "urn:expected"

    # A missing aud claim cannot satisfy an application-requested audience.
    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as absent_error:
        jwt.decode(
            _token({"sub": "user-123"}),
            SECRET,
            algorithms=["HS256"],
            audience=requested_audience,
        )

    # {"aud": null} is required to behave identically to an omitted aud claim.
    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as null_error:
        jwt.decode(
            _token({"sub": "user-123", "aud": None}),
            SECRET,
            algorithms=["HS256"],
            audience=requested_audience,
        )

    assert absent_error.value.claim == "aud"
    assert null_error.value.claim == "aud"

        {"sub": "user-123", "aud": None},
    ],
)
def test_null_audience_does_not_satisfy_a_required_audience_claim(payload):
    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as error:
        jwt.decode(
            _token(payload),
            SECRET,
            algorithms=["HS256"],
            options={"require": ["aud"]},
        )

    assert error.value.claim == "aud"

import jwt
from jwt.exceptions import InvalidAudienceError, MissingRequiredClaimError


SECRET = "secret"
ALGORITHMS = ["HS256"]


def _encode(payload):
    return jwt.encode(payload, SECRET, algorithm="HS256")

    "payload",
    [
        {"sub": "subject"},
        {"sub": "subject", "aud": None},
    ],
    ids=["aud-unspecified", "aud-null"],
)
def test_null_audience_is_accepted_without_audience_validation(payload):
    """An explicit JSON null audience must behave like an omitted audience."""
    token = _encode(payload)

    decoded = jwt.decode(token, SECRET, algorithms=ALGORITHMS)

    assert decoded == payload


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "audience",
    ["expected-audience", ["expected-audience"]],
    ids=["string-audience", "iterable-audience"],
)
def test_null_audience_behaves_like_missing_claim_when_audience_is_required(audience):
    """A null aud claim is unspecified, so it cannot satisfy an expected audience."""
    missing_aud_token = _encode({"sub": "subject"})
    null_aud_token = _encode({"sub": "subject", "aud": None})

    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as missing_error:
        jwt.decode(
            missing_aud_token,
            SECRET,
            algorithms=ALGORITHMS,
            audience=audience,
        )

    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as null_error:
        jwt.decode(
            null_aud_token,
            SECRET,
            algorithms=ALGORITHMS,
            audience=audience,
        )

    assert missing_error.value.claim == "aud"
    assert null_error.value.claim == "aud"

    """The null special case must not disable validation for real aud claims."""
    token = _encode({"sub": "subject", "aud": "actual-audience"})

    with pytest.raises(InvalidAudienceError):
        jwt.decode(token, SECRET, algorithms=ALGORITHMS)

from checkov.cloudformation.runner import Runner
from checkov.runner_filter import RunnerFilter


def _run_cloudformation(template_path, checks):
    return Runner().run(
        root_folder=None,
        files=[str(template_path)],
        runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=checks),
    )


def _security_group(name, ports):
    ingress_rules = "\n".join(
        f"""        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: {port}
          ToPort: {port}
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0"""
        for port in ports
    )
    return f"""  {name}:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: insecure test security group
      SecurityGroupIngress:
{ingress_rules}
"""


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_suppresses_issue_example_with_empty_reason(tmp_path):
    """The exact `#checkov:skip=CHECK_ID:` form from the issue must work."""
    template = tmp_path / "suppressed_ssh.yaml"
    template.write_text(
        """Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:
"""
        + _security_group("SecurityGroup", [22])
    )

    report = _run_cloudformation(template, ["CKV_AWS_24"])

    assert len(report.failed_checks) == 0
    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].resource == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SecurityGroup"


def test_cloudformation_resource_can_have_multiple_skip_comments(tmp_path):
    """Every annotation for a resource must be honored, not just the closest one."""
    template = tmp_path / "multiple_suppressions.yaml"
    template.write_text(
        """Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: SSH access is required for this test resource
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_25: RDP access is required for this test resource
"""
        + _security_group("OpenSecurityGroup", [22, 3389])
    )

    report = _run_cloudformation(template, ["CKV_AWS_24", "CKV_AWS_25"])

    assert len(report.failed_checks) == 0
    assert {record.check_id for record in report.skipped_checks} == {
        "CKV_AWS_24",
        "CKV_AWS_25",
    }
    assert {record.resource for record in report.skipped_checks} == {
        "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.OpenSecurityGroup"
    }

    skipped_by_id = {record.check_id: record for record in report.skipped_checks}
    assert skipped_by_id["CKV_AWS_24"].check_result["suppress_comment"] == (
        " SSH access is required for this test resource"
    )
    assert skipped_by_id["CKV_AWS_25"].check_result["suppress_comment"] == (
        " RDP access is required for this test resource"
    )


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_applies_only_to_its_resource(tmp_path):
    """A suppression for one CloudFormation resource must not suppress later ones."""
    template = tmp_path / "resource_scoped_suppression.yaml"
    template.write_text(
        """Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: This group intentionally permits SSH
"""
        + _security_group("SuppressedGroup", [22])
        + "\n"
        + _security_group("UnsuppressedGroup", [22])
    )

    report = _run_cloudformation(template, ["CKV_AWS_24"])

    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].resource == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SuppressedGroup"

    assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1
    assert report.failed_checks[0].resource == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.UnsuppressedGroup"

import pytest

from jwt.api_jwt import PyJWT
from jwt.exceptions import MissingRequiredClaimError


@pytest.fixture
def jwt():
    return PyJWT()


def test_null_audience_is_accepted_when_no_audience_is_requested(jwt):
    """A JSON null aud claim must not act like a populated aud claim."""
    payload = {"sub": "user-123", "aud": None}
    token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")

    assert jwt.decode(token, "secret", algorithms=["HS256"]) == payload


@pytest.mark.parametrize("audience", ["service-a", ["service-a", "service-b"]])
def test_null_audience_matches_missing_claim_when_audience_is_requested(jwt, audience):
    """An application-provided audience cannot be verified from null, just as
    it cannot be verified when aud is absent altogether.
    """
    null_audience_token = jwt.encode({"sub": "user-123", "aud": None}, "secret")
    missing_audience_token = jwt.encode({"sub": "user-123"}, "secret")

    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as null_error:
        jwt.decode(
            null_audience_token,
            "secret",
            audience=audience,
            algorithms=["HS256"],
        )

    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as missing_error:
        jwt.decode(
            missing_audience_token,
            "secret",
            audience=audience,
            algorithms=["HS256"],
        )

    assert null_error.value.claim == missing_error.value.claim == "aud"


def test_null_audience_remains_unverified_when_audience_verification_is_disabled(jwt):
    """Disabling audience verification must retain the behavior of an absent aud claim."""
    payload = {"sub": "user-123", "aud": None}
    token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")

    assert (
        jwt.decode(
            token,
            "secret",
            audience="service-a",
            algorithms=["HS256"],
            options={"verify_aud": False},
        )
        == payload
    )

import pytest

from jwt.api_jwt import PyJWT
from jwt.exceptions import MissingRequiredClaimError


SECRET = "secret"


def _token(payload):
    return PyJWT().encode(payload, SECRET, algorithm="HS256")


def test_decode_ignores_null_audience_when_no_audience_is_requested():
    jwt = PyJWT()
    payload = {"sub": "user-123", "aud": None}

    decoded = jwt.decode(_token(payload), SECRET, algorithms=["HS256"])

    # Validation must treat a JSON null audience as absent, without changing
    # the claims returned from the signed token.
    assert decoded == payload


@pytest.mark.parametrize("audience", ["expected-audience", ["expected-audience"]])
def test_null_audience_is_missing_when_an_audience_is_requested(audience):
    jwt = PyJWT()
    token = _token({"sub": "user-123", "aud": None})

    # An absent aud claim cannot satisfy a caller-supplied audience.  Since a
    # null aud is ignored, it must have the same MissingRequiredClaimError as
    # a token with no aud claim at all, rather than an invalid-format error.
    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
        jwt.decode(token, SECRET, algorithms=["HS256"], audience=audience)

    assert exc_info.value.claim == "aud"


def test_null_audience_does_not_satisfy_a_required_audience_claim():
    jwt = PyJWT(options={"require": ["aud"]})
    token = _token({"sub": "user-123", "aud": None})

    # Treating null as unspecified also means it cannot satisfy an explicit
    # requirement for the aud claim.
    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
        jwt.decode(token, SECRET, algorithms=["HS256"])

    assert exc_info.value.claim == "aud"

    def test_mpv_title_uses_equals_syntax_as_a_single_argument(self):
        # mpv 0.31+ rejects the legacy form:
        #     --title <value>
        # The value must instead be part of the same argument as --title=.
        self._test_args(
            [
                "streamlink",
                "-p",
                "/usr/bin/mpv",
                "--title",
                "{title}",
                "http://test.se",
                "test",
            ],
            ["/usr/bin/mpv", "--title=Test Title", "-"],
        )

    def test_mpv_title_with_quotes_is_not_shell_quoted_in_argv(self):
        # PlayerOutput passes an argv list to subprocess on POSIX. Shell quote
        # characters are therefore literal title characters, not quoting, and
        # must not be inserted around a title containing whitespace.
        self._test_args(
            [
                "streamlink",

                "/usr/bin/mpv",
                "--title",
                "O'Reilly's stream",
                "http://test.se",

            ],

_KEY = f"pytest-case-isolation-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"

    return fakeredis.FakeRedis()


def test_01_fixture_client_can_write_state(fake_redis_client):
    """The client created for one pytest case can use its own state."""
    assert fake_redis_client.keys("*") == []

    fake_redis_client.set(_KEY, "set in first pytest case")

    assert fake_redis_client.get(_KEY) == b"set in first pytest case"


def test_02_next_fixture_client_does_not_inherit_previous_case_state(fake_redis_client):
    """
    A newly-created default FakeRedis client for a later pytest case must not
    see keys written by the fixture client in the preceding case.
    """
    assert fake_redis_client.get(_KEY) is None
    assert _KEY.encode() not in fake_redis_client.keys("*")


def test_independently_created_default_sync_clients_are_isolated():
    """
    The fixture regression is caused by independent calls to FakeRedis(), so
    verify the behavior directly as well as across pytest fixture instances.
    """
    first = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
    second = fakeredis.FakeRedis()

    first.set(_KEY, "first client only")

    assert first.get(_KEY) == b"first client only"
    assert second.get(_KEY) is None

    """

    state between clients.

    first = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
    second = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)

    first.set(_KEY, "shared value")

        assert await first.get(_KEY) == b"async first client only"
        assert await second.get(_KEY) is None

        await first.aclose()
        await second.aclose()

import subprocess

import pytest

import streamlink_cli.output as output_module
from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title, escaped_title",
    [
        ("A title with spaces", "A title with spaces"),
        ('A "quoted" title', 'A "quoted" title'),
        ("O'Reilly & Friends", "O'Reilly & Friends"),
        ("Stream $HOME", "Stream $$HOME"),
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_is_one_raw_equals_argument_on_posix(monkeypatch, title, escaped_title):
    """
    On POSIX Streamlink invokes the player using an argv list, so shell quoting
    is not interpreted. mpv 0.31.1+ requires the title value to be attached to
    the long option with '=' and the argv entry must contain the title itself,
    rather than shell-quote characters.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", False)

    player = PlayerOutput(
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        args="{filename}",
        title=title,
        quiet=False,
    )

    assert player._create_arguments() == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        "--title={0}".format(escaped_title),
        "-",
    ]


def test_mpv_title_windows_command_uses_equals_before_windows_quoting(monkeypatch):
    """
    Windows command-line quoting must be performed by list2cmdline. POSIX
    shlex.quote output is not valid quoting for a Windows mpv command and
    would become part of the title value.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", True)

    title = "O'Reilly & Friends"
    player = PlayerOutput(
        "mpv.exe",
        args="{filename}",
        title=title,
        quiet=False,
    )

    expected = subprocess.list2cmdline([
        "mpv.exe",
        "--title={0}".format(title),
        "-",
    ])

    assert player._create_arguments() == expected

import textwrap

from checkov.cloudformation.runner import Runner
from checkov.runner_filter import RunnerFilter


def _run_cloudformation_template(tmp_path, content):
    template = tmp_path / "template.yaml"
    template.write_text(textwrap.dedent(content))

    return Runner().run(
        root_folder=None,
        files=[str(template)],
        runner_filter=RunnerFilter(framework="all", checks=["CKV_AWS_24"]),
    )


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_suppresses_only_annotated_resource(tmp_path):
    report = _run_cloudformation_template(
        tmp_path,
        """
        AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
        Resources:
          #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:SSH access is intentionally restricted elsewhere
          SuppressedSecurityGroup:
            Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
            Properties:
              GroupDescription: Group with an accepted SSH exception
              SecurityGroupIngress:
                - IpProtocol: tcp
                  FromPort: 22
                  ToPort: 22
                  CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0

          UnsuppressedSecurityGroup:
            Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
            Properties:
              GroupDescription: Group which must still be reported
              SecurityGroupIngress:
                - IpProtocol: tcp
                  FromPort: 22
                  ToPort: 22
                  CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
        """,
    )

    suppressed_resource = "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SuppressedSecurityGroup"
    unsuppressed_resource = "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.UnsuppressedSecurityGroup"

    assert any(
        record.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24" and record.resource == suppressed_resource
        for record in report.skipped_checks
    )
    assert not any(
        record.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24" and record.resource == suppressed_resource
        for record in report.failed_checks
    )

    # A suppression is resource-scoped; it must not suppress the same failed
    # check on another CloudFormation resource.
    assert any(
        record.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24" and record.resource == unsuppressed_resource
        for record in report.failed_checks
    )
    assert not any(
        record.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24" and record.resource == unsuppressed_resource
        for record in report.skipped_checks
    )

import pytest

import streamlink_cli.output as output_module
from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput


@pytest.mark.skipif(output_module.is_win32, reason="POSIX argv construction is tested separately")
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title",
    [
        "",
        "A title with spaces",
        """A title with "double" and 'single' quotes""",
        "A title with shell punctuation ; & |",
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_is_one_unquoted_equals_style_argv_argument(title):
    """
    mpv requires the --option=value form for long options. On POSIX,
    Streamlink invokes the player with an argv list, not a shell command, so
    shell-quoting characters must not become part of the title value.
    """
    player = PlayerOutput(
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        args="{filename}",
        title=title,
        quiet=False,
    )

    assert player._create_arguments() == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        "--title=" + title,
        "-",
    ]


def test_mpv_title_uses_equals_syntax_on_windows_command_line(monkeypatch):
    """
    The Windows command line is serialized after constructing the argument.
    Serialization can quote the whole argument for spaces, but POSIX quote
    characters must not have been embedded in the --title value.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", True)

    player = PlayerOutput(
        "mpv",
        args="{filename}",
        title="A title with spaces",
        quiet=False,
    )

    assert player._create_arguments() == 'mpv "--title=A title with spaces" -'

import pytest

import streamlink_cli.output as output_module
from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title",
    [
        "A stream title",
        'A title with "double quotes"',
        "O'Reilly's live stream",
        "title; with shell-looking characters & spaces",
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_is_passed_as_a_single_equals_style_argument(monkeypatch, title):
    """mpv's --title value must be attached with '=' and retain its exact value.

    On POSIX Streamlink invokes the player with an argv list, rather than a
    shell command. Shell quoting must therefore not be included in the argv
    item, since quote characters would become part of the title received by
    mpv.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", False)

    player = PlayerOutput(
        "mpv",
        args="{filename}",
        title=title,
        quiet=False,
    )

    assert player._create_arguments() == [
        "mpv",
        "--title=" + title,
        "-",
    ]


def test_mpv_title_keeps_equals_syntax_after_property_escaping(monkeypatch):
    """mpv property-expansion escaping must not revert to legacy option syntax."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", False)

    player = PlayerOutput(
        "mpv",
        args="{filename}",
        title="Price is $5",
        quiet=False,
    )

    assert player._create_arguments() == [
        "mpv",
        "--title=Price is $$5",
        "-",
    ]


def test_mpv_title_windows_command_has_equals_before_quoted_value(monkeypatch):
    """Windows command-line construction must also use --title=value syntax."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", True)

    player = PlayerOutput(
        "mpv.exe",
        args="{filename}",
        title="A stream title",
        quiet=False,
    )

    expected = "mpv.exe {0} -".format(
        subprocess.list2cmdline(["--title=A stream title"])
    )
    assert player._create_arguments() == expected

def test_qualified_source_hooks_work_without_installed_entry_points(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    """Hooks in the project's source tree must work before it is installed."""
    package_name = "ttg_uninstalled_project_hooks"
    package_dir = tmp_path / package_name
    package_dir.mkdir()

    (package_dir / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (package_dir / "versioning.py").write_text(
        """
def source_version_scheme(version):
    return "source-{0}.post{1}".format(version.tag, version.distance)


def source_local_scheme(version):
    return "+built-from-source"
"""
    )

    # There deliberately is no installed distribution/entry point for this
    # source package: it is only available because the project root is on
    # sys.path, as it is while setuptools is building the project.
    with pytest.raises(importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError):
        importlib.metadata.distribution(package_name)

    sys.path.insert(0, str(tmp_path))
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
    try:
        # A qualified hook must not need entry-point discovery at all.  In
        # particular, entry-point discovery cannot find hooks from the
        # distribution currently being built.
        def entry_points_must_not_be_used(*args, **kwargs):
            raise AssertionError("qualified source hooks attempted entry-point lookup")

        monkeypatch.setattr(
            "setuptools_scm._entrypoints.iter_entry_points",
            entry_points_must_not_be_used,
        )

        version_scheme = f"{package_name}.versioning.source_version_scheme"
        local_scheme = f"{package_name}.versioning.source_local_scheme"
        config = Configuration(
            version_scheme=version_scheme,
            local_scheme=local_scheme,
        )
        scm_version = meta(
            tag="1.2.3",
            distance=4,
            node="abcdef",
            dirty=False,
            config=config,
        )

        assert (
            format_version(
                scm_version,
                version_scheme=config.version_scheme,
                local_scheme=config.local_scheme,
            )
            == "source-1.2.3.post4+built-from-source"
        )
    finally:
        sys.path.remove(str(tmp_path))
        sys.modules.pop(package_name, None)
        sys.modules.pop(f"{package_name}.versioning", None)

def fake_redis_client():
    """Match the function-scoped client fixture from the reported regression."""
    client = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
    yield client
    client.close()


def test_default_clients_do_not_share_state():
    """Separate unconfigured FakeRedis clients must represent separate servers."""
    key = f"default-client-isolation:{uuid.uuid4()}"
    first_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
    second_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis()

    try:
        assert first_client.keys("*") == []
        assert second_client.keys("*") == []

        assert first_client.set(key, "value")
        assert first_client.get(key) == b"value"

        assert second_client.get(key) is None
        assert second_client.keys(key) == []
    finally:
        first_client.close()
        second_client.close()


def test_a_fixture_client_starts_empty_and_writes_state(fake_redis_client):
    """The first pytest fixture invocation writes data for the next test to detect."""
    assert fake_redis_client.keys("*") == []
    assert fake_redis_client.set(_FIXTURE_KEY, "written-by-test-a")
    assert fake_redis_client.keys(_FIXTURE_KEY) == [_FIXTURE_KEY.encode()]


def test_b_new_fixture_client_does_not_see_previous_test_state(fake_redis_client):
    """A new function-scoped fixture must not inherit test_a's Redis state."""
    assert fake_redis_client.keys("*") == []
    assert fake_redis_client.get(_FIXTURE_KEY) is None
    assert fake_redis_client.keys(_FIXTURE_KEY) == []


def test_explicit_fake_server_still_allows_intentional_sharing():
    """Isolation by default must not break the documented explicit sharing API."""
    server = fakeredis.FakeServer()
    first_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
    second_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
    key = f"explicit-server-sharing:{uuid.uuid4()}"

    try:
        assert first_client.set(key, "value")
        assert second_client.get(key) == b"value"
    finally:
        first_client.close()
        second_client.close()

import subprocess

import pytest

from streamlink_cli import output as output_module
from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title",
    [
        "",
        "A title with spaces",
        'A title with "double quotes" and \'single quotes\'',
        "A title with ; shell-like $characters",
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_is_one_literal_equals_style_argv_argument(monkeypatch, title):
    """
    On POSIX, subprocess receives an argv list rather than a shell command.
    Therefore quotes used for shell escaping must not be included in the value
    passed to mpv. mpv requires --title=<value>, as one argument.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", False)

    player = PlayerOutput(
        cmd="mpv",
        args="{filename}",
        title=title,
        quiet=False,
    )

    expected_title = PlayerOutput._mpv_title_escape(title)
    assert player._create_arguments() == [
        "mpv",
        "--title=" + expected_title,
        "-",
    ]


def test_mpv_title_uses_equals_syntax_on_windows_without_posix_shell_quotes(monkeypatch):
    """
    Windows performs its own command-line serialization via list2cmdline.
    POSIX shell quotes must not become part of mpv's --title value.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", True)

    title = 'Stream title with spaces and "quotes"'
    player = PlayerOutput(
        cmd="mpv",
        args="{filename}",
        title=title,
        quiet=False,
    )

    assert player._create_arguments() == subprocess.list2cmdline([
        "mpv",
        "--title=" + title,
        "-",
    ])

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from setuptools_scm import Configuration
from setuptools_scm.version import format_version, meta


def _version_with_config(version_scheme, local_scheme="no-local-version"):
    config = Configuration(
        version_scheme=version_scheme,
        local_scheme=local_scheme,
    )
    return meta(
        tag="1.2.3",
        distance=4,
        node="abcdef123456",
        dirty=False,
        config=config,
    )


def test_qualified_version_and_local_scheme_are_loaded_from_source_tree(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    """Qualified callables must work before the project has been installed."""
    package = tmp_path / "project_versioning"
    package.mkdir()
    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (package / "schemes.py").write_text(
        """
def version_scheme(version):
    return f"{version.tag}.source.{version.distance}"

def local_scheme(version):
    return "+loaded-from-source"
""".strip()
    )

    # This represents a source checkout being on sys.path during a build. The
    # project has not been installed and exposes no distribution entry points.
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))

    version = _version_with_config(
        "project_versioning.schemes.version_scheme",
        "project_versioning.schemes.local_scheme",
    )

    assert (
        format_version(
            version,
            version_scheme="project_versioning.schemes.version_scheme",
            local_scheme="project_versioning.schemes.local_scheme",
        )
        == "1.2.3.source.4+loaded-from-source"
    )


def test_get_version_can_import_a_scheme_from_an_uninstalled_project(tmp_path):
    """get_version must import a source package before it has an entry point."""
    if shutil.which("git") is None:
        pytest.skip("git is required to create an SCM-backed test project")

    project = tmp_path / "uninstalled-project"
    package = project / "build_versioning"
    package.mkdir(parents=True)
    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (package / "custom.py").write_text(
        """
def scheme(version):
    return f"{version.tag}.from-source.{version.distance}"
""".strip()
    )

    def git(*args):
        subprocess.check_call(
            ["git", *args],
            cwd=project,
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        )

    git("init")
    git("config", "user.email", "tests@example.invalid")
    git("config", "user.name", "Test User")
    git("add", ".")
    git("commit", "-m", "initial")
    git("tag", "1.0")

    (project / "README").write_text("one commit after the tag\n")
    git("add", "README")
    git("commit", "-m", "next")

    # Import setuptools_scm from this checkout, while the subprocess works in
    # an unrelated project's source tree. build_versioning is importable from
    # that source tree but is not installed and has no entry point.
    scm_source_root = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "src")
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = scm_source_root + os.pathsep + env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")

    result = subprocess.check_output(
        [
            sys.executable,
            "-c",
            (
                "from setuptools_scm import get_version; "
                "print(get_version(root='.', "
                "version_scheme='build_versioning.custom.scheme', "
                "local_scheme='no-local-version'))"
            ),
        ],
        cwd=project,
        env=env,
        text=True,
    ).strip()

    assert result == "1.0.from-source.1"


def test_existing_dotted_entry_point_names_keep_working(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """Qualified-name support must not break valid legacy entry-point names.

    Entry-point names are allowed to contain dots. Therefore an already
    configured entry point must continue to take precedence over an importable
    module that happens to have the same textual name. Falling back to a
    qualified import only when no such entry point exists both preserves legacy
    configurations and solves the source-tree chicken-and-egg problem.
    """
    import setuptools_scm._entrypoints as entrypoints

    package = tmp_path / "legacy_scheme"
    package.mkdir()
    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (package / "versioning.py").write_text(
        """
def scheme(version):
    return "imported-qualified-name"
""".strip()
    )
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))

    class FakeEntryPoint:
        name = "legacy_scheme.versioning.scheme"

        @staticmethod
        def load():
            def legacy_entry_point_scheme(version):
                return "loaded-entry-point"

            return legacy_entry_point_scheme

    original_iter_entry_points = entrypoints.iter_entry_points

    def iter_entry_points(group, name=None):
        if (
            group == "setuptools_scm.version_scheme"
            and name == "legacy_scheme.versioning.scheme"
        ):
            return iter((FakeEntryPoint(),))
        return original_iter_entry_points(group, name)

    monkeypatch.setattr(entrypoints, "iter_entry_points", iter_entry_points)

    version = _version_with_config("legacy_scheme.versioning.scheme")

    assert (
        format_version(
            version,
            version_scheme="legacy_scheme.versioning.scheme",
            local_scheme="no-local-version",
        )
        == "loaded-entry-point"
    )

import time
import warnings

import nltk


def test_unknown_characters_do_not_become_persistent_vowels():
    """Temporary vowel assignments must not mutate tokenizer configuration."""
    tokenizer = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    # Digits are the reported regression case. Other unknown phonemes used the
    # same state-mutating path and must likewise remain temporary.
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        for token in ("99", "1234567890", "abc123", "Ω"):
            tokenizer.tokenize(token)
            assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

        for _ in range(20):
            tokenizer.tokenize("99")

    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels


def test_numeric_tokenization_preserves_existing_output():
    """The performance fix must not change normal SSP tokenization results."""
    tokenizer = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]

    assert tokenizer.tokenize("justification") == [
        "jus",
        "ti",
        "fi",
        "ca",
        "tion",
    ]


def test_repeated_numbers_scale_approximately_linearly():
    """Repeated numeric tokenization must not become slower on every call.

    Previously, each unknown digit was appended to ``vowels``. Consequently,
    later calls searched an ever-growing regular expression and a tenfold
    increase in calls took dramatically more than ten times as long.
    """

    def duration(number_of_calls):
        tokenizer = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
            start = time.perf_counter()
            for _ in range(number_of_calls):
                tokenizer.tokenize("99")
            return time.perf_counter() - start

    short_run = duration(100)
    long_run = duration(1000)

    # Linear behavior should be near 10x. This deliberately allows substantial
    # CI timing noise, while the original quadratic regression is far larger.
    assert long_run / max(short_run, 1e-9) < 30, (
        "Repeated numeric tokenization grew superlinearly: "
        f"100 calls took {short_run:.6f}s but 1000 calls took {long_run:.6f}s"
    )

import streamlink_cli.output as output_module
from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title, expected_title",
    [
        ("A title with spaces", "A title with spaces"),
        ("--this-must-remain-a-title", "--this-must-remain-a-title"),
        ("", ""),
        ("Price is $5", "Price is $$5"),
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_is_passed_as_a_single_equals_option_on_posix(monkeypatch, title, expected_title):
    """mpv >= 0.31 rejects '--title VALUE'; its value must be part of the option."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", False)

    player = PlayerOutput(
        "mpv",
        args="{filename}",
        title=title,
        quiet=False,
    )

    assert player._create_arguments() == [
        "mpv",
        "--title=" + expected_title,
        "-",
    ]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("title", ["A title with spaces", "--not-an-mpv-option"])
def test_mpv_title_uses_equals_syntax_in_windows_command_line(monkeypatch, title):
    """Windows command-line serialization must not turn the title into a separate argv item."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", True)

    player = PlayerOutput(
        "mpv.exe",
        args="{filename}",
        title=title,
        quiet=False,
    )

    expected_title_argument = subprocess.list2cmdline(["--title=" + title])
    assert player._create_arguments() == "mpv.exe {0} -".format(expected_title_argument)

import time
import warnings

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


def test_repeated_numeric_tokens_do_not_accumulate_duplicate_vowels():
    """Repeated unknown numeric characters must not make tokenizer state grow."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        for _ in range(50):
            tokenizer.tokenize("99")
            tokenizer.tokenize("0123456789")

    # Implementations may either keep unknown characters temporary or cache them,
    # but repeated occurrences must never be appended repeatedly.  Such duplicate
    # growth is what made repeated numeric tokenization quadratic.
    for digit in "0123456789":
        assert tokenizer.vowels.count(digit) <= 1

    # Tokenization must continue to preserve all characters in a numeric token.
    assert "".join(tokenizer.tokenize("0123456789")) == "0123456789"


def test_repeated_numeric_tokenization_completes_promptly():
    """The reported repeated-'99' workload should no longer degrade quadratically."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(1000):
            assert "".join(tokenizer.tokenize("99")) == "99"
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start

    # This leaves substantial room for slow CI while rejecting the former
    # state-growing implementation, whose cost rises sharply over this loop.
    assert elapsed < 2.0, f"repeated numeric tokenization was too slow: {elapsed:.3f}s"

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

def source_tree_scheme(version):
    """A scheme used through its importable qualified name."""
    return f"{version.tag}.post{version.distance}"


def _run(command, cwd, env=None):
    completed = subprocess.run(
        command,
        cwd=cwd,
        env=env,
        text=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
    )
    assert completed.returncode == 0, (
        f"command failed: {' '.join(map(str, command))}\n"
        f"stdout:\n{completed.stdout}\n"
        f"stderr:\n{completed.stderr}"
    )
    return completed


def _setuptools_scm_from_checkout_environment():
    """Use the checkout under test, without adding a test project to PYTHONPATH."""
    env = os.environ.copy()
    old_pythonpath = env.get("PYTHONPATH")
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = (
        str(SOURCE_ROOT)
        if not old_pythonpath
        else str(SOURCE_ROOT) + os.pathsep + old_pythonpath
    )
    return env

import warnings

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


def test_numeric_characters_are_temporary_vowels_and_do_not_mutate_tokenizer():
    """Repeated numeric tokenization must not grow persistent vowel state."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)

        # This is deliberately repeated: the historical implementation appended
        # each unknown digit to ``vowels`` on every call, causing later calls to
        # become progressively slower.
        for _ in range(250):
            assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]

    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels


def test_multi_digit_tokens_keep_their_syllabification_without_state_leakage():
    """Unknown digits still act as vowels for the current token only."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)

        # Digits are unknown to the default English hierarchy, but are assigned
        # maximum sonority for the token being processed.  Preserve the existing
        # syllable boundaries while ensuring that assignment is not retained.
        assert tokenizer.tokenize("123") == ["12", "3"]
        assert tokenizer.tokenize("456") == ["45", "6"]

    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels


def test_numeric_processing_does_not_affect_later_word_tokenization():
    """Processing many numbers must not change normal tokenizer behavior."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        for _ in range(100):
            tokenizer.tokenize("99")

    assert tokenizer.tokenize("justification") == [
        "jus",
        "ti",
        "fi",
        "ca",
        "tion",
    ]
    assert tokenizer.vowels == "aeiouy"

import time
import warnings

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


def _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, token):
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        return tokenizer.tokenize(token)


def test_numbers_are_temporary_vowels_and_do_not_mutate_tokenizer_configuration():
    """Unknown numeric characters must not be retained in ``vowels`` between calls."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    # Preserve the established treatment of unknown characters as vowels for the
    # current token while ensuring that this treatment is not persistent.
    assert _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "99") == ["99"]
    assert _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "123") == ["12", "3"]

    # Repeated values are the case that formerly appended duplicate digits to
    # self.vowels and made later calls progressively slower.
    for _ in range(50):
        _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "99")

    # Different digits must not be retained either.
    for token in ("0", "1234567890", "9876543210", "42"):
        _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, token)

    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels


def test_unknown_characters_do_not_change_later_tokenization_or_vowels():
    """Temporary unknown vowels must not leak into later mixed tokens."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    expected = _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "a1b2")
    assert expected == ["a1", "b2"]
    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

    # Processing many unrelated unknown characters must neither grow the public
    # configuration nor change the result for an earlier token.
    for token in ("3", "7", "99", "x8y", "456", "z0"):
        _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, token)

    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels
    assert _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "a1b2") == expected


def test_number_processing_does_not_mutate_custom_hierarchy_vowels():
    """The non-mutating guarantee applies to custom sonority hierarchies too."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer(sonority_hierarchy=["a", "b"])
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    for _ in range(20):
        _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "1029384756")

    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels == "a"


def test_repeated_numbers_complete_in_reasonable_time():
    """Repeated numeric tokens must not exhibit the former quadratic slowdown."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(1500):
            tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start

    # This is deliberately generous for loaded CI workers.  The old behavior
    # grows self.vowels on every call and spends seconds compiling/searching an
    # ever-growing regular expression, whereas a non-mutating implementation is
    # substantially faster.
    assert elapsed < 2.0
    assert tokenizer.vowels == "aeiouy"

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title, expected_title",
    [
        ("A title with spaces", "A title with spaces"),

)
def test_mpv_title_is_passed_as_a_single_equals_option_on_posix(title, expected_title, monkeypatch):
    """mpv >= 0.31 requires --title's value to be attached with '='."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", False)

    player = PlayerOutput(
        "/usr/bin/mpv --cache 2048",
        args="{filename}",
        title=title,
        quiet=False,
    )

    assert player._create_arguments() == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        "--cache",
        "2048",
        "--title={0}".format(expected_title),
        "-",
    ]


def test_mpv_title_equals_syntax_is_preserved_in_windows_command_line(monkeypatch):

    player = PlayerOutput(
        "mpv.exe",
        args="{filename}",
        title="A title with spaces",
        quiet=False,
    )
