import importlib.util
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path


def _run(*args: str, cwd: Path) -> None:
    subprocess.run(
        args,
        cwd=cwd,
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
    )


def test_pyproject_can_load_uninstalled_package_qualified_version_scheme(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    """A build can import a dotted scheme from the project currently being built.

    The function has no setuptools entry point and its package is deliberately
    not installed. This is the chicken-and-egg case described by the issue:
    setuptools_scm needs the function while generating project metadata, before
    the project can have been installed.
    """
    project = tmp_path / "project"
    package = project / "uninstalled_scheme_project"
    package.mkdir(parents=True)

    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (package / "versioning.py").write_text(
        textwrap.dedent(
            """\
            def custom_version_scheme(version):
                # A distinct result proves that this source-tree callable, and
                # not a built-in setuptools_scm version scheme, was used.
                return f"{version.tag}.post{version.distance}"
            """
        )
    )
    (project / "pyproject.toml").write_text(
        textwrap.dedent(
            """\
            [build-system]
            requires = ["setuptools", "setuptools_scm"]
            build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

            [project]
            name = "qualified-scheme-build-test"
            dynamic = ["version"]

            [tool.setuptools_scm]
            version_scheme = "uninstalled_scheme_project.versioning.custom_version_scheme"
            local_scheme = "no-local-version"
            """
        )
    )

    _run("git", "init", cwd=project)
    _run("git", "config", "user.email", "test@example.invalid", cwd=project)
    _run("git", "config", "user.name", "Test User", cwd=project)
    _run("git", "add", ".", cwd=project)
    _run("git", "commit", "-m", "initial", cwd=project)
    _run("git", "tag", "1.2.3", cwd=project)

    # Make the SCM version non-exact, ensuring that the scheme receives and uses
    # its distance argument.
    (project / "README.md").write_text("next commit\n")
    _run("git", "add", "README.md", cwd=project)
    _run("git", "commit", "-m", "next", cwd=project)

    # The project package has no installed distribution or entry point, and the
    # temporary project root has not been placed on this test process's sys.path.
    assert importlib.util.find_spec("uninstalled_scheme_project") is None

    wheel_dir = tmp_path / "wheels"
    wheel_dir.mkdir()
    completed = subprocess.run(
        [
            sys.executable,
            "-m",
            "pip",
            "wheel",
            "--no-build-isolation",
            "--no-deps",
            "--no-index",
            "--wheel-dir",
            str(wheel_dir),
            str(project),
        ],
        check=False,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
    )

    assert completed.returncode == 0, (
        "Generating build metadata must import a dotted custom version scheme "
        "from the uninstalled project's source tree.\n"
        f"stdout:\n{completed.stdout}\n\nstderr:\n{completed.stderr}"
    )

    wheels = list(wheel_dir.glob("qualified_scheme_build_test-*.whl"))
    assert len(wheels) == 1

    with zipfile.ZipFile(wheels[0]) as wheel:
        metadata_name = next(
            name for name in wheel.namelist() if name.endswith(".dist-info/METADATA")
        )
        metadata = wheel.read(metadata_name).decode()

    assert "Version: 1.2.3.post1\n" in metadata

import time
import warnings

import nltk


def test_numeric_tokens_keep_their_syllabification_across_repeated_calls():
    """Unknown numeric characters must continue to be handled as vowels."""
    tokenizer = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

        # All three unknown digits are assigned maximum sonority.  Preserve the
        # resulting syllabification rather than regressing to treating the token
        # as a word with no vowels.
        assert tokenizer.tokenize("123") == ["12", "3"]

        first_result = tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        for _ in range(100):
            assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == first_result

    assert first_result == ["99"]


def test_repeated_numeric_tokens_do_not_keep_growing_tokenizer_state():
    """Repeated input must not accumulate configuration indefinitely."""
    tokenizer = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        tokenizer.tokenize("123")
        vowels_after_first_use = tokenizer.vowels

        for _ in range(200):
            tokenizer.tokenize("123")

    # A correct implementation may keep unknown characters in a bounded cache,
    # or may use temporary per-token vowel information.  Either way, processing
    # exactly the same number repeatedly must not continue extending `vowels`.
    assert tokenizer.vowels == vowels_after_first_use


def test_repeated_numeric_tokenization_remains_fast():
    """Regression test for the reported quadratic slowdown on ``tokenize('99')``."""
    tokenizer = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

        assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
        vowels_before_timing = tokenizer.vowels

        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(1500):
            tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start

    # The original implementation appends two more "9" characters on every
    # call, making its regex and vowel-count work increasingly expensive.  The
    # fixed implementation completes this workload in milliseconds; this limit
    # is intentionally generous for slow CI machines while still rejecting the
    # quadratic behavior.
    assert elapsed < 1.5
    assert tokenizer.vowels == vowels_before_timing

import time
import warnings

import nltk


def _tokenize_silently(tokenizer, token):
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        return tokenizer.tokenize(token)


def test_unknown_numeric_characters_do_not_mutate_configured_vowels():
    """Unknown characters are temporary vowel assignments, not tokenizer state."""
    tokenizer = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    # Reuse the same tokenizer, as in the reported timeit example.  Numbers,
    # mixed tokens, and distinct unknown characters must not permanently extend
    # the configured vowel inventory.
    for token in ("99", "1234567890", "abc123", "987", "42"):
        syllables = _tokenize_silently(tokenizer, token)
        assert "".join(syllables) == token
        assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

    # The public attribute should remain the original configured string rather
    # than a progressively accumulated sequence of digits.
    assert tokenizer.vowels == "aeiouy"


def test_numbers_keep_unknown_as_temporary_vowels_without_state_leakage():
    """Removing the mutation must retain the prior unknown-character behavior."""
    tokenizer = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    # Each unknown digit is assigned maximum sonority for this token.  The
    # resulting syllabification must be stable across calls, even though no
    # digit is retained in ``vowels``.
    first = _tokenize_silently(tokenizer, "123")
    assert first == ["12", "3"]
    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

    for _ in range(20):
        assert _tokenize_silently(tokenizer, "123") == first
        assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels


def test_repeated_numbers_are_fast_on_one_reused_tokenizer():
    """Repeated numeric tokenization must not degrade as tokenizer state grows."""
    tokenizer = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(1200):
            assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start

    # A correct implementation has fixed vowel state and completes this well
    # below the limit; the historical accumulating-vowels implementation shows
    # the reported quadratic slowdown at this scale.
    assert elapsed < 1.5
    assert tokenizer.vowels == "aeiouy"

import warnings

import pytest

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


class CountTrackingString(str):
    """A string that records how often its count method is scanned."""

    def __new__(cls, value):
        instance = super().__new__(cls, value)
        instance.count_calls = 0
        return instance

    def count(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.count_calls += 1
        return super().count(*args, **kwargs)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("number", ["99", "0123456789"])
def test_repeated_numeric_tokens_do_not_cause_growing_vowel_scans(number):
    """Numeric tokens must remain linear-time when the tokenizer is reused.

    ``SyllableTokenizer.tokenize`` uses ``token.count`` while checking for
    vowels.  Repeatedly extending its vowel collection with unknown digits
    makes the number of such scans grow on every call, producing the reported
    quadratic slowdown.  A fixed implementation may retain newly seen digits,
    but the amount of work per call must stay bounded.
    """
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    token = CountTrackingString(number)
    repetitions = 80

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        results = [tokenizer.tokenize(token) for _ in range(repetitions)]

    assert all(isinstance(result, list) for result in results)

    # English starts with six vowels; even an implementation that remembers
    # each of the ten decimal digits needs at most sixteen count calls per
    # token.  Leave room for equivalent constant-time implementations.
    assert token.count_calls <= repetitions * 25

        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        values = tokenizer.assign_values("9")

def test_repeated_numeric_tokenization_has_linear_call_scaling():
    """Later batches of number tokenization should not get progressively slower."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    def tokenize_many(count):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(count):
            tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        return time.perf_counter() - start

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

        # The first batch also initializes any implementation-specific caches.
        tokenize_many(20)
        first_batch = tokenize_many(80)
        later_batch = tokenize_many(400)

    # than becoming much slower as the tokenizer's state grows.

import time
import warnings

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


def _time_repeated_numeric_tokenization(iterations):
    """Time repeated tokenization of the numeric input from the regression."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        # Digits are intentionally outside the default sonority hierarchy.
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)

        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(iterations):
            assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
        return time.perf_counter() - start


def test_syllable_tokenizer_numeric_input_scales_linearly_across_calls():
    """
    Repeated numeric inputs must not become progressively more expensive.

    Historically, tokenizing unknown numeric characters appended them to the
    tokenizer's vowel string.  Each subsequent call then performed more work
    when counting vowels, making a batch of calls quadratic in its size.
    """
    small_batch_time = _time_repeated_numeric_tokenization(50)
    large_batch_time = _time_repeated_numeric_tokenization(500)

    # A ten-times-larger batch should remain approximately linear.  The
    # generous allowance accommodates slow or temporarily loaded CI workers,
    # while the former quadratic behavior exceeds this substantially.
    assert large_batch_time <= small_batch_time * 40 + 0.05


def test_syllable_tokenizer_can_repeatedly_process_all_numeric_characters():
    """Unknown digits remain valid token inputs over repeated calls."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        for digit in "0123456789":
            for _ in range(20):
                assert tokenizer.tokenize(digit) == [digit]

def test_pyproject_qualified_version_scheme_loads_from_uninstalled_project_source(
    tmp_path,
):
    """A pyproject version scheme can import project source before installation.

    The project deliberately provides no setuptools entry point.  Its custom
    scheme is only reachable as ``package.module:function`` while setuptools
    is producing metadata/wheels, i.e. before that project has been installed.
    """
    if shutil.which("git") is None:
        pytest.skip("git is required to create a repository for setuptools_scm")

    project = tmp_path / "project"
    package = project / "source_version_project"
    package.mkdir(parents=True)

    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (package / "versioning.py").write_text(
        """
def version_from_project_source(version):
    # A local-version suffix makes it unambiguous that this function, rather
    # than a built-in or an entry point, supplied the version.
    return f"{version.tag}+fromprojectsource"
""".lstrip()
    )

    (project / "pyproject.toml").write_text(
        """
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools", "setuptools_scm"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "qualified-name-build-test"
dynamic = ["version"]

[tool.setuptools_scm]
version_scheme = "source_version_project.versioning:version_from_project_source"
local_scheme = "no-local-version"
""".lstrip()
    )

    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PIP_NO_INDEX"] = "1"
    env["PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK"] = "1"

    # Ensure the subprocess executes the checkout under test, even if another
    # setuptools_scm happens to be installed in site-packages.
    source_root = str(Path(setuptools_scm.__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = source_root + os.pathsep + env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")

    for command in (
        ["git", "init"],
        ["git", "config", "user.email", "tests@example.invalid"],
        ["git", "config", "user.name", "setuptools_scm tests"],
        ["git", "add", "."],
        ["git", "commit", "-m", "initial"],
        ["git", "tag", "v7.4.0"],
    ):
        result = _run(command, cwd=project, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout

    wheel_dir = tmp_path / "wheels"
    result = _run(
        [
            sys.executable,
            "-m",
            "pip",
            "wheel",
            "--no-build-isolation",
            "--no-deps",
            "--wheel-dir",
            str(wheel_dir),
            ".",
        ],
        cwd=project,
        env=env,
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout

    wheels = list(wheel_dir.glob("*.whl"))
    assert len(wheels) == 1

    with zipfile.ZipFile(wheels[0]) as wheel:
        metadata_name = next(
            name for name in wheel.namelist() if name.endswith(".dist-info/METADATA")
        )
        metadata = wheel.read(metadata_name).decode()

    assert "Version: 7.4.0+fromprojectsource" in metadata

from typing import Tuple

import numpy as np
import pytest

from supervision.detection.utils import move_masks


def expected_translated_masks(
    masks: np.ndarray, offset: np.ndarray, resolution_wh: Tuple[int, int]
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Independently translate every source pixel, dropping out-of-frame pixels."""
    width, height = resolution_wh
    dx, dy = map(int, offset)
    expected = np.zeros((masks.shape[0], height, width), dtype=bool)

    for source_y in range(masks.shape[1]):
        destination_y = source_y + dy
        if not 0 <= destination_y < height:
            continue

        for source_x in range(masks.shape[2]):
            destination_x = source_x + dx
            if 0 <= destination_x < width:
                expected[:, destination_y, destination_x] = masks[
                    :, source_y, source_x
                ]

    return expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("offset", "resolution_wh"),
    [
        pytest.param(
            np.array([-1, -2]),
            (2, 1),
            id="negative_offset_crops_left_top_and_output_right",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            np.array([2, 1]),
            (4, 3),
            id="positive_offset_crops_right_and_bottom",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            np.array([2, -1]),
            (5, 3),
            id="positive_x_negative_y_crops_top_and_right",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            np.array([-2, 1]),
            (3, 3),
            id="negative_x_positive_y_crops_left_and_bottom",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_move_masks_translates_all_masks_and_crops_at_frame_boundaries(
    offset: np.ndarray, resolution_wh: Tuple[int, int]
) -> None:
    # Asymmetric patterns make source/destination slice errors visible, and two
    # masks verify that translation is applied independently to every prediction.
    masks = np.array(
        [
            [
                [True, False, True, False],
                [False, True, False, False],
                [True, True, False, True],
            ],
            [
                [False, True, False, True],
                [True, False, True, False],
                [False, False, True, True],
            ],
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )

    result = move_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=offset,
        resolution_wh=resolution_wh,
    )

    expected = expected_translated_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    assert result.shape == (masks.shape[0], resolution_wh[1], resolution_wh[0])
    assert result.dtype == np.bool_
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(result, expected)


def test_move_masks_accepts_negative_offsets_without_cropping() -> None:
    masks = np.array(
        [
            [
                [False, False, False, False],
                [False, True, False, True],
                [True, False, True, False],
                [False, True, True, False],
            ]
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )
    offset = np.array([-1, -1])

    result = move_masks(masks=masks, offset=offset, resolution_wh=(4, 4))

    expected = expected_translated_masks(masks, offset, (4, 4))
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(result, expected)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "offset",
    [
        pytest.param(np.array([-10, 0]), id="entirely_left"),
        pytest.param(np.array([0, -10]), id="entirely_above"),
        pytest.param(np.array([10, 0]), id="entirely_right"),
        pytest.param(np.array([0, 10]), id="entirely_below"),
    ],
)
def test_move_masks_returns_empty_masks_when_moved_fully_outside_frame(
    offset: np.ndarray,
) -> None:
    masks = np.array(
        [
            [
                [True, False],
                [False, True],
            ]
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )

    result = move_masks(masks=masks, offset=offset, resolution_wh=(3, 3))

    assert result.shape == (1, 3, 3)
    assert result.dtype == np.bool_
    assert not result.any()

from supervision.detection.utils import move_masks


def _expected_translation(
    masks: np.ndarray, offset: np.ndarray, resolution_wh: tuple[int, int]

    """Independent reference for translating masks with output-boundary cropping."""
    width, height = resolution_wh
    dx, dy = offset
    expected = np.zeros((masks.shape[0], height, width), dtype=bool)

    for source_y in range(masks.shape[1]):

        if not 0 <= destination_y < height:
            continue

        for source_x in range(masks.shape[2]):
            destination_x = source_x + dx
            if 0 <= destination_x < width:

                    :, source_y, source_x
                ]

    return expected

)

import numpy as np
import pytest

from supervision.detection.utils import move_masks


def expected_moved_masks(
    masks: np.ndarray, offset: np.ndarray, resolution_wh: tuple
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Build translated masks by mapping every destination pixel to its source."""
    output_width, output_height = resolution_wh
    expected = np.zeros((masks.shape[0], output_height, output_width), dtype=bool)

    dx, dy = offset
    for output_y in range(output_height):
        for output_x in range(output_width):
            source_y = output_y - dy
            source_x = output_x - dx
            if 0 <= source_y < masks.shape[1] and 0 <= source_x < masks.shape[2]:
                expected[:, output_y, output_x] = masks[:, source_y, source_x]

    return expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "offset,resolution_wh",
    [
        # Negative movement crops source pixels beyond the top-left boundary.
        (np.array([-2, -1]), (5, 4)),
        # Mixed movement crops at the top and right boundaries.
        (np.array([2, -1]), (4, 3)),
        # Mixed movement crops at the left and bottom boundaries.
        (np.array([-1, 2]), (3, 4)),
        # Moving entirely outside the destination produces empty masks.
        (np.array([10, -10]), (4, 3)),
    ],
)
def test_move_masks_translates_in_all_directions_and_crops_to_resolution(
    offset: np.ndarray, resolution_wh: tuple
) -> None:
    masks = np.array(
        [
            [
                [True, False, True, False, False],
                [False, True, False, True, False],
                [True, True, False, False, True],
                [False, False, True, True, False],
            ],
            [
                [False, True, False, True, True],
                [True, False, True, False, True],
                [False, False, True, True, False],
                [True, True, False, False, True],
            ],
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )

    result = move_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=offset,
        resolution_wh=resolution_wh,
    )

    expected = expected_moved_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=offset,
        resolution_wh=resolution_wh,
    )

    assert result.dtype == np.bool_
    assert result.shape == expected.shape
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(result, expected)


def test_move_masks_negative_offset_preserves_visible_source_values() -> None:
    masks = np.array(
        [
            [
                [False, False, False, False],
                [False, True, False, True],
                [True, False, True, False],
                [False, True, True, False],
            ]
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )

    result = move_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=np.array([-1, -2]),
        resolution_wh=(4, 4),
    )

    expected = np.array(
        [
            [
                [False, True, False, False],
                [True, True, False, False],
                [False, False, False, False],
                [False, False, False, False],
            ]
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )

    np.testing.assert_array_equal(result, expected)

import numpy as np
import pytest

from supervision.detection.utils import move_masks


def expected_translation(
    masks: np.ndarray, offset: tuple[int, int], resolution_wh: tuple[int, int]
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Translate masks by (dx, dy), retaining only pixels within the output frame."""
    dx, dy = offset
    output_width, output_height = resolution_wh
    _, input_height, input_width = masks.shape

    expected = np.zeros((masks.shape[0], output_height, output_width), dtype=bool)

    source_x_start = max(0, -dx)
    source_x_stop = min(input_width, output_width - dx)
    source_y_start = max(0, -dy)
    source_y_stop = min(input_height, output_height - dy)

    if source_x_start < source_x_stop and source_y_start < source_y_stop:
        expected[
            :,
            source_y_start + dy : source_y_stop + dy,
            source_x_start + dx : source_x_stop + dx,
        ] = masks[
            :,
            source_y_start:source_y_stop,
            source_x_start:source_x_stop,
        ]

    return expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "offset,resolution_wh",
    [
        pytest.param((-1, -1), (4, 3), id="negative-offset-crops-top-left"),
        pytest.param(
            (-2, -1),
            (3, 2),
            id="negative-offset-also-crops-at-output-bottom-right",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            (2, -2),
            (4, 3),
            id="mixed-sign-offset-crops-on-opposite-edges",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            (2, 2),
            (3, 2),
            id="positive-offset-crops-at-output-bottom-right",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            (-10, 0),
            (4, 3),
            id="mask-moved-completely-outside-output",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_move_masks_translates_and_clips_for_any_offset_direction(
    offset: tuple[int, int], resolution_wh: tuple[int, int]
) -> None:
    # Deliberately asymmetric values make an incorrect crop or translation visible.
    masks = np.array(
        [
            [
                [False, True, False, True, False],
                [True, False, True, False, True],
                [False, True, True, False, False],
                [True, False, False, True, True],
            ]
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )
    original_masks = masks.copy()

    result = move_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=np.asarray(offset, dtype=np.int32),
        resolution_wh=resolution_wh,
    )

    expected = expected_translation(
        masks=original_masks,
        offset=offset,
        resolution_wh=resolution_wh,
    )

    assert result.shape == (1, resolution_wh[1], resolution_wh[0])
    assert result.dtype == np.bool_
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(result, expected)
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(masks, original_masks)


def test_move_masks_applies_negative_offset_to_every_mask() -> None:
    masks = np.array(
        [
            [
                [True, False, False],
                [False, True, False],
                [False, False, True],
            ],
            [
                [False, False, True],
                [False, True, False],
                [True, False, False],
            ],
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )
    offset = (-1, 1)
    resolution_wh = (3, 3)

    result = move_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=np.asarray(offset, dtype=np.int32),
        resolution_wh=resolution_wh,
    )

    expected = expected_translation(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    assert result.shape == (2, 3, 3)
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(result, expected)

import numpy as np
import pytest

from supervision.detection.utils import move_masks


def _expected_translation(
    masks: np.ndarray, offset: tuple[int, int], resolution_wh: tuple[int, int]
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Translate foreground pixels, dropping pixels outside the output canvas."""
    width, height = resolution_wh
    dx, dy = offset
    expected = np.zeros((masks.shape[0], height, width), dtype=bool)

    for mask_index, source_y, source_x in zip(*np.nonzero(masks)):
        destination_x = source_x + dx
        destination_y = source_y + dy
        if 0 <= destination_x < width and 0 <= destination_y < height:
            expected[mask_index, destination_y, destination_x] = True

    return expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("masks", "offset", "resolution_wh"),
    [
        pytest.param(
            np.array(
                [

                        [True, False, True, False],
                        [False, True, False, True],
                    ]

                dtype=bool,

            (4, 3),
            id="negative_offset_crops_top_and_left",

                        [True, True, False],

                ],
                dtype=bool,
            ),

            id="negative_x_and_positive_y_crops_left_and_bottom",

) -> None:

    np.testing.assert_array_equal(result, expected)
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(masks, original_masks)

def expected_translated_masks(

) -> np.ndarray:

    width, height = resolution_wh
    dx, dy = offset
    expected = np.zeros((masks.shape[0], height, width), dtype=bool)

    for mask_index, mask in enumerate(masks):
        for source_y, source_x in zip(*np.where(mask)):
            target_x = source_x + dx
            target_y = source_y + dy
            if 0 <= target_x < width and 0 <= target_y < height:
                expected[mask_index, target_y, target_x] = True

    return expected

    """Negative x/y offsets shift masks up and left, cropping outside pixels."""
    masks = np.array(
        [
            [
                [True, False, False, True],
                [False, True, True, False],
                [True, True, False, False],
            ],
            [
                [False, True, False, True],
                [True, False, True, False],
                [False, False, True, True],
            ],
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )

    moved = move_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=np.array([-1, -1]),
        resolution_wh=(4, 3),
    )

    expected = np.array(
        [
            [
                [True, True, False, False],
                [True, False, False, False],
                [False, False, False, False],
            ],
            [
                [False, True, False, False],
                [False, True, True, False],
                [False, False, False, False],
            ],
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )

    np.testing.assert_array_equal(moved, expected)
    assert moved.dtype == np.bool_


def test_move_masks_supports_negative_x_with_positive_y_offset() -> None:
    """Offsets may have independently signed x and y components."""
    masks = np.array(
        [
            [
                [True, False, False, True],
                [False, True, True, False],
                [True, True, False, False],
            ]
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )

    moved = move_masks(
        masks=masks,

    alias = headers

def test_mutable_headers_ior_matches_update_semantics_for_existing_headers():
    headers = MutableHeaders({"Keep": "original", "Replace": "old"})
    # A MutableHeaders instance may contain duplicates when append() is used.
    headers.append("replace", "duplicate")

    headers |= {"REPLACE": "new", "X-Added": "added"}

    # Existing unrelated headers are retained, replacement is case-insensitive,
    # duplicates are removed just as they are by MutableHeaders.update(), and
    # new headers are appended.
    assert headers.items() == [
        ("keep", "original"),
        ("replace", "new"),
        ("x-added", "added"),
    ]

    headers = MutableHeaders({"Content-Type": "text/plain"})
    original_raw = headers.raw[:]
    alias = headers

    headers |= {}

    assert headers is alias
    assert headers.raw == original_raw
